For each $n\geq 1$ , the functions $\eta_{n,e}$ and $\eta_{n,s,j}$ satisfy the following properties:

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}+\delta_{j}\rVert^{n+1}p_{j\mid z}-\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n+1}-\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp})=O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}), \displaystyle\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}-\delta_{j}\rVert^{n+1}-\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n+1}+\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{\perp})=O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}), \displaystyle\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp}+\delta)-\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp})=\Theta(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}),\text{ for all $\lVert\delta\rVert\leq 1$} \displaystyle\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{\perp}-\delta)-\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{\perp})=\Theta(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}),\text{ for all $\lVert\delta\rVert\leq 1$} \displaystyle-\mathcal{A}f_{n}(x)=-\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp})\cdot\alpha^{{(r)}}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{\perp})\cdot\mu_{j}\mathbbm{1}{\left(z_{j}>0\right)}\geq b\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n}, $$

with $b=\mu_{\min}/2\sqrt{J}$ for JSQ policy and $b=\mu_{\Sigma}p_{\min}^{2}/(2\sqrt{J})$ for Po2 policy.

Applying the test function $f_{n}$ in (5.2) to BAR (4.3) and utilizing (5.15), the left-hand side of (4.3) becomes

$$ -\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\mathcal{A}f(X^{{(r)}})\right]\geq b\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{n}]. $$

On the right-hand side of the BAR (4.3) corresponding to the external arrival, the increment conditional on the pre-jump state $x_{-}=(z_{-},r_{-,e},r_{-,s})$ is

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n}(x_{+})-f_{n}(x_{-})\right]=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n}(x_{-}+\Delta_{e,\ell})\right]p_{\ell\mid z}-f(x_{-}) \displaystyle=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\Big[\frac{1}{n+1}\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n+1}-\eta_{n,e}(z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell})\cdot\mathbb{E}[T_{e}]+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell})\cdot\mu_{j}r_{s,j}\Big]p_{\ell\mid z}-f(x_{-}) \displaystyle=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{1}{n+1}\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n+1}p_{\ell\mid z}-\frac{1}{n+1}\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n+1}-\eta_{n,e}(z_{-,\perp}) \displaystyle\quad+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\left[\eta_{n,e}(z_{-,\perp})-\eta_{n,e}(z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell})\right]p_{\ell\mid z}+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left[\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell})-\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{-,\perp})\right]\mu_{j}r_{s,j}p_{\ell\mid z} \displaystyle=O(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}O(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})r_{-,s,j}=O(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})+O(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})\psi_{1}, $$

where the second equality holds since $T_{e}$ and $X^{{(r)}}_{-}$ are independent in Lemma 4, the third equality holds due to $\mathbb{E}[T_{e}]=1$ , and the last equality follows from (5.11) and (5.13) in Lemma 6. Taking the expectation under $\mathbb{P}_{e}$ , the right-hand side of (4.3) corresponding to the external arrival becomes

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[f_{n}(X_{+}^{{(r)}})-f_{n}(X_{-}^{{(r)}})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n}(x_{+})-f_{n}(x_{-})\mid X_{-}^{{(r)}}=x_{-}\right]\right] \displaystyle\quad=\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[O(\lVert Z^{{(r)}}_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})\right]+\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[O(\lVert Z^{{(r)}}_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})\psi_{1}\right]\leq\Theta_{1}. $$

Since Hölder’s inequality indicates that $\mathbb{E}_{e}[O(\lVert Z^{{(r)}}_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})\psi_{1}]\leq\mathbb{E}_{e}[O(\lVert Z^{{(r)}}_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})]^{(M-n)/(M-n+1)}\cdot$ $\mathbb{E}_{e}[O(\lVert Z^{{(r)}}_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})\psi_{1}^{M-n+1}]^{1/(M-n+1)}$ , the inequality in (5.17) follows from the induction hypotheses (S2) and (S4) for $n-1$ , and $\Theta_{1}$ is a positive constant independent of $r$ .

On the right-hand side of the BAR (4.3) corresponding to the service completion at station $\ell\in\mathcal{J}$ , the increment conditional on the pre-jump state $x_{-}=(z_{-},r_{-,e},r_{-,s})$ is

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n}(x_{+})-f_{n}(x_{-})\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n}(x_{-}+\Delta_{s,\ell})\right]-f(x_{-}) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n+1}\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n+1}-\eta_{n,e}(z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell})\cdot\alpha^{{(r)}}r_{-,e}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J},j\neq\ell}\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell})\cdot\mu_{j}r_{-,s,j} \displaystyle+\eta_{n,s,\ell}(z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell})\cdot\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}]-\Big[\frac{1}{n+1}\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n+1}-\eta_{n,e}(z_{-,\perp})\cdot\alpha^{{(r)}}r_{-,e}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J},j\neq\ell}\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{-,\perp})\cdot\mu_{j}r_{-,s,j}\Big] \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n+1}\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n+1}-\frac{1}{n+1}\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n+1}+\eta_{n,s,\ell}(z_{-,\perp})+\eta_{n,s,\ell}(z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell})-\eta_{n,s,\ell}(z_{-,\perp}) \displaystyle\quad+\left(\eta_{n,e}(z_{-,\perp})-\eta_{n,e}(z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell})\right)\cdot\alpha^{{(r)}}r_{-,e}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J},j\neq\ell}\left(\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell})-\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{-,\perp})\right)\cdot\mu_{j}r_{-,s,j} \displaystyle=O(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})+O(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})r_{-,e}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J},j\neq\ell}O(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})r_{-,s,j}=O(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})+O(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})\psi_{1}, $$

where the second equality follows from the fact that $T_{s,\ell}$ and $X^{{(r)}}_{-}$ are independent in Lemma 4, the third equality holds due to $\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}]=1$ , and the last equality follows from (5.12) and (5.14) in Lemma 6. Taking the expectation under $\mathbb{P}_{s,\ell}$ , the right-hand side of (4.3) that corresponds to the service completion at station $\ell$ becomes

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[f_{n}(X_{+}^{{(r)}})-f_{n}(X_{-}^{{(r)}})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n}(x_{+})-f_{n}(x_{-})\mid X_{-}^{{(r)}}=x_{-}\right]\right] \displaystyle\quad=\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[O(\lVert Z^{{(r)}}_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})\right]+\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[O(\lVert Z^{{(r)}}_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})\psi_{1}\right]\leq\Theta_{2}, $$

where the inequality follows from the induction hypotheses (S2) and (S4) for $n-1$ , and $\Theta_{2}$ is a positive constant independent of $r$ .

In summary, combining (5.16), (5.17) and (5.18), the BAR (4.3) implies that

$$ b\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right]\leq\alpha^{{(r)}}\Theta_{1}+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\lambda^{{(r)}}\Theta_{2}=\left(\Theta_{1}+\Theta_{2}\right)\alpha^{{(r)}}\leq\left(\Theta_{1}+\Theta_{2}\right)\mu_{\Sigma}, $$

which completes the proof of (S1) for the induction step $n$ .

### 5.4 Proof of (S2)

Based on the induction hypotheses, we assume that Statement (S1) holds for $0,1\ldots,n$ , and Statements (S2)-(S4) are satisfied for $0,1,\ldots,n-1$ . We will now demonstrate the validity of Statement (S2) for the induction step $n$ by substituting $f_{n,D}$ as defined in (5.3) into the BAR (4.3).

On the left-hand side of the BAR (4.3), we have

$$ -\mathcal{A}f_{n,D}(x)=\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n}\left(1+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbbm{1}{\left(z_{j}>0\right)}\right)\leq(J+1)\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n}, $$

and hence, the left-hand side of the BAR (4.3) becomes

$$ -\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\mathcal{A}f_{n,D}\left(X^{{(r)}}\right)\right]\leq(J+1)\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right]\leq(J+1)C_{n}, $$

where the last inequality follows from the induction hypothesis (S1) for $n$ .

On the right-hand side of the BAR (4.3) corresponding to the external arrival, conditioning on the pre-jump state $x_{-}=(z_{-},r_{-,e},r_{-,s})$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[f_{n,D}(x_{+})-f_{n,D}(x_{-})] \displaystyle=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,D}(x_{-}+\Delta_{e,\ell})\right]p_{\ell\mid z}-f_{n,D}(x_{-}) \displaystyle=\left(\psi_{1}+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{e}]}{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\right)\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}p_{\ell\mid z}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{1} \displaystyle=\left(\psi_{1}+\frac{1}{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\right)\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\left(\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\right)p_{\ell\mid z}+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\frac{1}{\alpha^{{(r)}}} \displaystyle=\left(\psi_{1}+\frac{1}{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\right)\Theta(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\frac{1}{\alpha^{{(r)}}}, $$

where the second equality follows from the fact that $T_{e}$ and $X^{{(r)}}_{-}$ are independent in Lemma 4, the third equality holds by $\mathbb{E}[T_{e}]=1$ , and the last equality follows from (5.13). Taking the expectation under $\mathbb{P}_{e}$ , the right-hand side of (4.3) that corresponds to the external arrival becomes

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[f_{n,D}(X^{{(r)}}_{+})-f_{n,D}(X^{{(r)}}_{-})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,D}(x_{+})-f_{n,D}(x_{-})\mid X_{-}^{{(r)}}=x_{-}\right]\right] \displaystyle\quad=\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left(\psi_{1}+\frac{1}{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\right)\Theta(\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{n-1})\right]+\frac{1}{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right]\geq-\Theta_{3}+\frac{1}{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right], $$

where the last inequality holds by the induction hypotheses (S2) and (S4) for $n-1$ , and $\Theta_{3}$ is a positive constant independent of $r$ .

On the right-hand side of the BAR (4.3) corresponding to the service completion at station $\ell$ , conditional on the pre-jump state $x_{-}=(z_{-},r_{-,e},r_{-,s})$ , the increment of $f_{n,D}$ is

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[f_{n,D}(x_{+})-f_{n,D}(x_{-})]=\mathbb{E}[f_{n,D}(x_{-}+\Delta_{s,\ell})-f_{n,D}(x_{-})]=\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}\left(\psi_{1}+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}]}{\mu_{\ell}}\right)-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{1} \displaystyle\quad=\left(\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\right)\left(\psi_{1}+\frac{1}{\mu_{\ell}}\right)+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\frac{1}{\mu_{\ell}}=\Theta(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})\left(\psi_{1}+\frac{1}{\mu_{\ell}}\right)+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\frac{1}{\mu_{\ell}}, $$

where the second equality follows from the fact that $T_{s,\ell}$ and $X^{{(r)}}_{-}$ are independent in Lemma 4, the third equality holds by $\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}]=1$ , and the last equality follows from (5.14). Taking the expectation under $\mathbb{P}_{s,\ell}$ , the right-hand side of (4.3) that corresponds to the service completion at station $\ell$ becomes

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[f_{n,D}(X^{{(r)}}_{+})-f_{n,D}(X^{{(r)}}_{-})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,D}(x_{+})-f_{n,D}(x_{-})\mid X_{-}^{{(r)}}=x_{-}\right]\right] \displaystyle\quad=\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[O(\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{n-1})\left(\psi_{1}+\frac{1}{\mu_{\ell}}\right)\right]+\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\frac{1}{\mu_{\ell}}\right]\geq-\Theta_{4}+\frac{1}{\mu_{\ell}}\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right], $$

where the last inequality holds by the induction hypotheses (S2) and (S4) for $n-1$ , and $\Theta_{4}$ is a positive constant independent of $r$ .

In summary, combining (5.19), (5.20) and (5.21), the BAR (4.3) implies that

$$ \displaystyle(J+1)C_{n}\geq-\alpha^{{(r)}}\Theta_{3}+\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right]+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\lambda^{{(r)}}_{\ell}\left(-\Theta_{4}+\frac{1}{\mu_{\ell}}\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right]\right) \displaystyle\geq-\alpha^{{(r)}}\left(\Theta_{3}+\Theta_{4}\right)+\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right]+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{\mu_{\ell}-r}{\mu_{\ell}}\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right], $$

where the last inequality follows from $\lambda^{{(r)}}_{\Sigma}=\alpha^{{(r)}}$ and (5.9).

Therefore, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right]+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right] \displaystyle\leq\frac{(J+1)C_{n}+\alpha^{{(r)}}\left(\Theta_{3}+\Theta_{4}\right)}{\min_{\ell\in\mathcal{J},r\in(0,r_{0})}\frac{\mu_{\ell}-r}{\mu_{\ell}}}\leq\frac{(J+1)C_{n}+\left(\Theta_{3}+\Theta_{4}\right)\mu_{\Sigma}}{\frac{\mu_{\min}-r_{0}}{\mu_{\max}}}, $$

which completes the proof of (S2) for the induction step $n$ .

### 5.5 Proof of (S3)

Building upon the induction hypotheses, we assume that Statements (S1) and (S2) hold for $0,1,\ldots,n$ , while Statements (S3) and (S4) are satisfied for $0,1,\ldots,n-1$ . In this section, we aim to prove Statement (S3) for the induction step $n$ . Note that when $n=M$ , Statement (S3) holds trivially due to Statement (S1). Hence, in the subsequent analysis, we will solely focus on the cases when $1\leq n<M$ .

Plugging $f_{n,E}$ in (5.4) into BAR (4.3), the left-hand side becomes

$$ -\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\mathcal{A}f\left(X^{{(r)}}\right)\right]=(M-n+1)\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\left(\left(R_{e}^{{(r)}}\right)^{M-n}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(R_{s,j}^{{(r)}}\right)^{M-n}\mathbbm{1}{\left(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}>0\right)}\right)\right]. $$

On the right-hand side of the BAR (4.3) corresponding to the external arrival, conditional on the pre-jump state $x_{-}=(z_{-},r_{-,e},r_{-,s})$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,E}(x_{+})-f_{n,E}(x_{-})\right]=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,E}(x_{-}+\Delta_{e,\ell})\right]p_{\ell\mid z}-f_{n,E}(x_{-}) \displaystyle\quad=\left(\psi_{M-n+1}+\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{T_{e}}{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\right)^{M-n+1}\right]\right)\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}p_{\ell\mid z}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n+1} \displaystyle\quad=\left(\psi_{M-n+1}+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{e}^{M-n+1}]}{(\alpha^{{(r)}})^{M-n+1}}\right)\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\left(\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\right)p_{\ell\mid z}+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{e}^{M-n+1}]}{(\alpha^{{(r)}})^{M-n+1}} \displaystyle\quad=\left(\psi_{M-n+1}+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{e}^{M-n+1}]}{(\alpha^{{(r)}})^{M-n+1}}\right)O(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{e}^{M-n+1}]}{(\alpha^{{(r)}})^{M-n+1}}, $$

where the second equality follows from the fact that $T_{e}$ and $X^{{(r)}}_{-}$ are independent in Lemma 4, and the last equality follows from (5.13). Taking the expectation under $\mathbb{P}_{e}$ , the right-hand side of (4.3) that corresponds to the external arrival becomes

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[f_{n,E}(X^{{(r)}}_{+})-f_{n,E}(X^{{(r)}}_{-})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,E}(x_{+})-f_{n,E}(x_{-})\mid X_{-}^{{(r)}}=x_{-}\right]\right] \displaystyle\quad=\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left(\psi_{M-n+1}+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{e}^{M-n+1}]}{(\alpha^{{(r)}})^{M-n+1}}\right)\Theta(\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{n-1})\right]+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{e}^{M-n+1}]}{(\alpha^{{(r)}})^{M-n+1}}\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right]\leq\Theta_{5} $$

where the last inequality holds by the induction hypotheses (S2) for $n-1$ and $n$ together with (S4) for $n-1$ , and $\Theta_{5}$ is a positive constant independent of $r$ .

On the right-hand side of the BAR (4.3) corresponding to the service completion at station $\ell$ , conditional on the pre-jump state $x_{-}=(z_{-},r_{-,e},r_{-,s})$ , the increment of $f_{n,E}$ is

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,E}(x_{+})-f_{n,E}(x_{-})\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,E}(x_{-}+\Delta_{s,\ell})\right]-f_{n,E}(x_{-}) \displaystyle=\left(\psi_{M-n+1}+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}^{M-n+1}]}{\mu_{\ell}^{M-n+1}}\right)\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n+1} \displaystyle=\left(\psi_{M-n+1}+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}^{M-n+1}]}{\mu_{\ell}^{M-n+1}}\right)\left(\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\right)+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}^{M-n+1}]}{\mu_{\ell}^{M-n+1}} \displaystyle=\left(\psi_{M-n+1}+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}^{M-n+1}]}{\mu_{\ell}^{M-n+1}}\right)\Theta(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1})+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}^{M-n+1}]}{\mu_{\ell}^{M-n+1}}, $$

where the second equality follows from the fact that $T_{s,\ell}$ and $X^{{(r)}}_{-}$ are independent in Lemma 4, and the last equality follows from (5.14). Taking the expectation under $\mathbb{P}_{s,\ell}$ , the right-hand side of (4.3) that corresponds to the service completion at station $\ell$ becomes

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[f_{n,E}(X^{{(r)}}_{+})-f_{n,E}(X^{{(r)}}_{-})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,E}(x_{+})-f_{n,E}(x_{-})\mid X_{-}^{{(r)}}=x_{-}\right]\right] \displaystyle\quad=\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left(\psi_{M-n+1}+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}^{M-n+1}]}{\mu_{\ell}^{M-n+1}}\right)\Theta(\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{n-1})\right]+\frac{\mathbb{E}[T_{s,\ell}^{M-n+1}]}{\mu_{\ell}^{M-n+1}}\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\right]\leq\Theta_{6}, $$

where the last inequality holds by the induction hypotheses (S2) for $n-1$ and $n$ together with (S4) for $n-1$ , and $\Theta_{6}$ is a positive constant independent of $r$ .

In summary, combining (5.22), (5.23) and (5.24), the BAR (4.3) implies that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\left(\left(R_{e}^{{(r)}}\right)^{M-n}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(R_{s,j}^{{(r)}}\right)^{M-n}\mathbbm{1}{\left(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}>0\right)}\right)\right] \displaystyle\leq\frac{\alpha^{{(r)}}\Theta_{5}+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\lambda^{{(r)}}_{\ell}\Theta_{6}}{M-n+1}\leq\frac{\left(\Theta_{5}+\Theta_{6}\right)\mu_{\Sigma}}{M-n+1}. $$

Following the model setting in (2.3), the residual service time $R^{(r)}_{s,j}(t)$ is set to the service time of the next job to be processed at station $j$ if $Z_{j}^{{(r)}}(t)=0$ . Thus, $R^{(r)}_{s,j}(t)$ is independent of the $\sigma$ -algebra $\mathcal{F}_{t-}^{X^{{(r)}}}$ , and hence is independent of $Z^{{(r)}}(t)$ . Conditional on the event $\{Z_{j}^{(r)}=0\}$ under $\pi$ , $R_{s,j}^{(r)}$ has the same distribution as ${T_{s,j}}/{\mu_{j}}$ and is independent of $Z^{{(r)}}$ . Therefore, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\left(R_{s,j}^{{(r)}}\right)^{M-n}\mathbbm{1}{\left(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right)}\right]=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\frac{\mathbb{E}[T^{M-n}_{s,j}]}{\mu^{M-n}_{j}}\mathbbm{1}{\left(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right)}\right]\leq C_{n}\frac{\mathbb{E}[T^{M+1}_{s,j}]^{\frac{M-n}{M+1}}}{\mu^{M-n}_{j}}, $$

where the last inequality holds by the induction hypothesis (S1) for $n$ , and hence,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right] \displaystyle\leq\frac{\left(\Theta_{5}+\Theta_{6}\right)\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mu_{j}}{M-n+1}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}C_{n}\frac{\mathbb{E}[T^{M+1}_{s,j}]^{\frac{M-n}{M+1}}}{\mu^{M-n}_{j}}, $$

which completes the proof of (S3) for the induction step $n$ .

### 5.6 Proof of (S4)

Given the induction hypotheses, we assume that Statements (S1)-(S3) hold for $0,1,\ldots,n$ , and Statement (S4) is satisfied for $0,1,\ldots,n-1$ . We will now prove Statement (S4) for the induction step $n$ . However, if $n=M$ , Statement (S4) is trivially satisfied due to Statement (S2). Therefore, in the following analysis, we will focus on the cases where $1\leq n<M$ .

On the left side of the BAR (4.3), we have

$$ \displaystyle-\mathcal{A}f_{n,F}(x) \displaystyle=\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\left(1+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbbm{1}{\left(z_{j}>0\right)}\right)\psi_{M-n}+(M-n)\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\left(r_{e}^{M-n-1}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}r_{s,j}^{M-n-1}\mathbbm{1}{\left(z_{j}>0\right)}\right)\psi_{1} \displaystyle\leq(J+1)\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}+(M-n)\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{1}\psi_{M-n-1}\leq\left(2J+4J^{2}M\right)\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}, $$

where the last inequality holds due to the property stated in (5.8). Hence, the left-hand side of the BAR (4.3) becomes

$$ \displaystyle-\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\mathcal{A}f\left(X^{{(r)}}\right)\right]\leq(2J+4J^{2}M)\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right]\leq(2J+4J^{2}M)E_{n}, $$

where the final inequality follows from the induction hypothesis (S3) for $n$ .

On the right-hand side of the BAR (4.3) corresponding to the external arrival, conditional on the pre-jump state $x_{-}=(z_{-},r_{-,e},r_{-,s})$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,F}(x_{+})-f_{n,F}(x_{-})\right]=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,F}(x_{-}+\Delta_{e,\ell})\right]p_{\ell\mid z}-f_{n,F}(x_{-}) \displaystyle\quad=\left(\psi_{M-n}+\mathbb{E}\left[\left({T_{e}}/{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\right)^{M-n}\right]\right)\left(\psi_{1}+\mathbb{E}\left[{T_{e}}/{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\right]\right)\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}p_{\ell\mid z}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\psi_{1} \displaystyle\quad\geq\psi_{M-n}\left(\psi_{1}+{1}/{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\right)\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\left(\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}+\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\right)p_{\ell\mid z}+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}/{\alpha^{{(r)}}} \displaystyle\quad=\Theta(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\psi_{M-n+1})+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}/{\alpha^{{(r)}}}, $$

where the second equality follows from the fact that $T_{e}$ and $X^{{(r)}}_{-}$ are independent in Lemma 4, and the last inequality follows from (5.13). Taking the expectation under $\mathbb{P}_{e}$ , the right-hand side of (4.3) that corresponds to the external arrival becomes

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[f_{n,F}(X^{{(r)}}_{+})-f_{n,F}(X^{{(r)}}_{-})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,F}(x_{+})-f_{n,F}(x_{-})\mid X_{-}^{{(r)}}=x_{-}\right]\right] \displaystyle~=\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\Theta(\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{n-1}\psi_{M-n+1})\right]+\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right]/{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\geq-\Theta_{7}+\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right]/{\alpha^{{(r)}}}, $$

where the last inequality holds by the induction hypothesis (S4) for $n-1$ , and $\Theta_{7}$ is a positive constant independent of $r$ .

On the right-hand side of the BAR (4.3) corresponding to the service completion at station $\ell$ , conditional on the pre-jump state $x_{-}=(z_{-},r_{-,e},r_{-,s})$ , the increment of $f_{n,F}$ is

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,F}(x_{+})-f_{n,F}(x_{-})\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,F}(x_{-}+\Delta_{s,\ell})\right]-f_{n,F}(x_{-}) \displaystyle=\left(\psi_{M-n}+\mathbb{E}\left[\left({T_{s,\ell}}/{\mu_{\ell}}\right)^{M-n}\right]\right)\left(\psi_{1}+\mathbb{E}\left[{T_{s,\ell}}/\mu_{\ell}\right]\right)\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\psi_{1} \displaystyle\geq\psi_{M-n}\left(\psi_{1}+1/{\alpha^{{(r)}}}\right)\left(\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}-\delta_{\ell}\right\rVert^{n}-\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\right)+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}/\mu_{\ell} \displaystyle=\Theta(\lVert z_{-,\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\psi_{M-n+1})+\left\lVert z_{-,\perp}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}/{\mu_{\ell}}, $$

where the second equality follows from the fact that $T_{s,\ell}$ and $X^{{(r)}}_{-}$ are independent in Lemma 4, and the last equality follows from (5.14). Taking the expectation under $\mathbb{P}_{s,\ell}$ , the right-hand side of the BAR (4.3) that corresponds to the service completion at station $\ell$ becomes

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[f_{n,F}(X^{{(r)}}_{+})-f_{n,F}(X^{{(r)}}_{-})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[f_{n,F}(x_{+})-f_{n,F}(x_{-})\mid X_{-}^{{(r)}}=x_{-}\right]\right] \displaystyle~=\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\Theta(\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{n-1}\psi_{M-n+1})\right]+\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right]/\mu_{\ell}\geq-\Theta_{8}+\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right]/\mu_{\ell}, $$

where the last inequality holds by the induction hypothesis (S4) for $n-1$ , and $\Theta_{8}$ is a positive constant independent of $r$ .

In summary, combining (5.25), (5.26) and (5.27), the BAR (4.3) implies that

$$ \displaystyle[2J+4J^{2}M]E_{n}\geq\alpha^{{(r)}}\Theta_{7}+\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right]+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\lambda^{{(r)}}_{\ell}\left(\Theta_{8}+\frac{1}{\mu_{\ell}}\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right]\right) \displaystyle\geq-\alpha^{{(r)}}\left(\Theta_{7}+\Theta_{8}\right)+\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right]+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{\mu_{\ell}-r}{\mu_{\ell}}\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right], $$

where the last inequality follows from $\lambda^{{(r)}}_{\Sigma}=\alpha^{{(r)}}$ and (5.9).

Therefore, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right]+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\left\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{n}\psi_{M-n}\right] \displaystyle\leq\frac{(2J+4J^{2}M)E_{n}+\alpha^{{(r)}}\left(\Theta_{7}+\Theta_{8}\right)}{\min_{\ell\in\mathcal{J},r\in(0,r_{0})}\frac{\mu_{\ell}-r}{\mu_{\ell}}} \displaystyle\leq\frac{(2J+4J^{2}M)E_{n}+\left(\Theta_{3}+\Theta_{4}\right)\mu_{\Sigma}}{\frac{\mu_{\min}-r_{0}}{\mu_{\max}}}, $$

which completes the proof of (S4) for the induction step $n$ .

### 5.7 Proof of Non-integer Case when $\varepsilon>0$

To prove Proposition 5 when $\varepsilon>0$ , it is essential to introduce the following lemma, which aligns directly with Statements (S1)-(S4) in Section 5.1 by replacing $M$ with $\beta\equiv M+\varepsilon/(M+\varepsilon)$ and substituting $n$ with $\beta-1$ .

#### Lemma 7.

Under the moment condition (5.1), there exist positive and finite constants $C_{\beta-1}$ , $D_{\beta-1}$ , $E_{\beta-1}$ and $F_{\beta-1}$ independent of $r$ such that the following statements hold for all $r\in(0,r_{0})$ :

- (1) $\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{\beta-1}]\leq C_{\beta-1}$ .

- (2) $\mathbb{E}_{e}[\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{\beta-1}]+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbb{E}_{{s,\ell}}[\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{\beta-1}]\leq D_{\beta-1}$ .

- (3) $\mathbb{E}_{\pi}[\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{\beta-1}\psi_{1}(R_{e}^{{(r)}},R_{s}^{{(r)}})]\leq E_{\beta-1}$ .

- (4) $\mathbb{E}_{e}[\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{\beta-1}\psi_{1}(R_{-,e}^{{(r)}},R_{-,s}^{{(r)}})]+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbb{E}_{{s,\ell}}[\lVert Z_{-,\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{\beta-1}\psi_{1}(R_{-,e}^{{(r)}},R_{-,s}^{{(r)}})]\leq F_{\beta-1}$ .

To prove Statements (1)-(4), we need to introduce the following lemma, which directly corresponds to the base step of Statements (S3)-(S4) when $n=0$ .

#### Lemma 8.

Under the moment condition (5.1), there exist positive and finite constants $A_{1}$ and $A_{2}$ independent of $r$ such that the following statements hold for all $r\in(0,r_{0})$ :

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\psi_{M+\varepsilon}\left(R_{e}^{(r)},R_{s}^{(r)}\right)\right]\leq A_{1} \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[\psi_{M+\varepsilon}\left(R_{-,e}^{(r)},R_{-,s}^{(r)}\right)\right]+\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{J}}\mathbb{E}_{s,\ell}\left[\psi_{M+\varepsilon}\left(R_{-,e}^{(r)},R_{-,s}^{(r)}\right)\right]\leq A_{2} $$

#### Proof of Lemma 8.

The proof of Lemma 8 follows the same approach as presented in Section 5.2. Specifically, the proof of (5.28) can directly adopt the proof approach of Statement (S3) in Section 5.2 by replacing $M$ with $M+\varepsilon$ in the test function (5.6). Similarly, the proof of (5.29) can directly adopt the proof approach of Statement (S4) in Section 5.2 by replacing $M$ with $M+\varepsilon$ in the test function (5.7). ∎

#### Proof of Lemma 7.

Since Proposition 5 for integer cases when $\varepsilon=0$ implies that Statements (S1) and (S2) hold for $n=M$ , Statements (1) and (2) also hold due to $\beta-1<M$ . Statement (3) can be established as follows:

$$ \mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{\beta-1}\psi_{1}\right]\leq\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{M}\right]^{1-\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\psi_{1}^{M+\varepsilon}\right]^{\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}\leq C_{M}^{1-\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}\cdot 2JA_{1}^{\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}, $$

where the first inequality holds due to Hölder’s inequality, and the second inequality follows from Lemma 8 and the fact that $\psi_{1}^{M+\varepsilon}\leq(2JR_{\max}^{{(r)}})^{M+\varepsilon}\leq(2J)^{M+\varepsilon}\psi_{M+\varepsilon}$ with $R_{\max}^{{(r)}}\equiv\max(\{R_{e}^{(r)}\}\cup\{R_{s,j}^{(r)}:j\in\mathcal{J}\})$ . Consequently, $E_{\beta-1}$ can be set as $2JC_{M}^{1-\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}A_{1}^{\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}$ . Statement (4) follows the same argument as (5.30) by replacing $\pi$ to any Palm measure $\nu$ in $\{\mathbb{P}_{e}\}\cup\{\mathbb{P}_{s,\ell};\ell\in\mathcal{J}\}$ :

$$ \mathbb{E}_{\nu}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{\beta-1}\psi_{1}\right]\leq\mathbb{E}_{\nu}\left[\left\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\right\rVert^{\beta-1}\right]^{1-\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}\mathbb{E}_{\nu}\left[\psi_{1}^{M+\varepsilon}\right]^{\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}\leq D_{M}^{1-\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}\cdot 2JA_{2}^{\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}. $$

Consequently, $F_{k,\beta-1}$ can be set as $4J^{2}D_{M}^{1-\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}A_{2}^{\frac{1}{M+\varepsilon}}$ . ∎

#### Proof of Proposition 5.

The proof of Proposition 5 parallels the approach in Section 5.3, with only two changes: substituting $n$ with $\beta$ and replacing Statements (S1)-(S4) with Statements (1)-(4). ∎

## 6 Proof of Steady-state Convergence in Proposition 3

In this section, we prove the weak convergence of the steady-state average queue length in Proposition 3. For simplicity, we equivalently prove the weak convergence of the steady-state total queue length $r\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}Z_{j}^{{(r)}}\Rightarrow JZ^{*}$ as $r\rightarrow 0$ . Our proof heavily follows the proof in Braverman et al. (2024).

### 6.1 Test Function for the BAR

In the transform method by Hurtado-Lange and Maguluri (2020), they utilize the exponential function $g_{\theta}$ for any $\theta\leq 0$ as

$$ g_{\theta}(z)=e^{\theta\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}z_{j}},\quad z\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}^{J}. $$

Incorporating truncation on residual interarrival and service times for $t>0$ , we define the test function $f^{{(r)}}_{\theta,t}$ for $\theta\leq 0$ and $t>0$ as

$$ f^{{(r)}}_{\theta,t}(x)=g_{\theta}(z)e^{-\xi_{e}(\theta,t)(\alpha^{{(r)}}r_{e}\wedge t^{-1})-\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\xi_{s,j}(\theta,t)(\mu_{j}r_{s,j}\wedge t^{-1})},~x=(z,r_{e},r_{s})\in\mathbb{S}, $$

where $\xi_{e}(\theta,t)$ and $\xi_{s,j}(\theta,t)$ for $j\in\mathcal{J}$ are the solutions to

$$ e^{\theta}\mathbb{E}_{e}\left[e^{-\xi_{e}(\theta,t)(T_{e}\wedge t^{-1})}\right]=1,\quad e^{-\theta}\mathbb{E}_{s,j}\left[e^{-\xi_{s,j}(\theta,t)(T_{s,j}\wedge t^{-1})}\right]=1\quad\text{ for }j\in\mathcal{J}. $$

The functions $\xi_{e}(\theta,t)$ and $\xi_{s,j}(\theta,t)$ for $j\in\mathcal{J}$ are uniquely determined by (6.1), which can be proved in Lemma C.1 of Braverman et al. (2024). Hence, the jump terms in the BAR (4.3) will be zero, i.e.,

$$ \mathbb{E}_{e}\left[f^{{(r)}}_{\theta,t}(X^{{(r)}}_{+})-f^{{(r)}}_{\theta,t}(X^{{(r)}}_{-})\right]=0,\quad\mathbb{E}_{s,j}\left[f^{{(r)}}_{\theta,t}(X^{{(r)}}_{+})-f^{{(r)}}_{\theta,t}(X^{{(r)}}_{-})\right]=0\quad\text{ for }j\in\mathcal{J}. $$

Therefore, applying the test function $f^{{(r)}}_{\theta,t}$ to the BAR (4.3) yields

$$ \mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\mathcal{A}f^{{(r)}}_{\theta,t}(X^{{(r)}})\right]=0. $$

We are now ready to define two sets of moment generating functions (MGFs) for $Z^{{(r)}}$ and $X^{{(r)}}$ as follows. For $Z^{{(r)}}$ , we define, for each $\theta\leq 0$ and $r\in(0,1)$ ,

$$ \phi^{{(r)}}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[g_{\theta}(Z^{{(r)}})\right]\quad\phi^{{(r)}}_{j}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[g_{\theta}(Z^{{(r)}})\mid Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right]\quad\text{ for }j\in\mathcal{J}, $$

Note that $\phi^{{(r)}}(r\eta)$ , $\eta<0$ , is the MGF of the scaled total queue length $r\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}{Z}^{{(r)}}_{j}$ .

For $X^{{(r)}}$ , we set $t=r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}}$ where $\varepsilon_{0}\in(0,\delta_{0}/(1+\delta_{0}))$ , which is consistent with SSC result in Proposition 2, and define truncated MGFs as

$$ \psi^{{(r)}}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[f^{{(r)}}_{\theta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}}}(X^{{(r)}})\right],\quad\psi^{{(r)}}_{j}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[f^{{(r)}}_{\theta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}}}(X^{{(r)}})\mid Z_{j}^{{(r)}}=0\right]\quad\text{ for }j\in\mathcal{J}. $$

### 6.2 Outline of the Proof

In this section, we will prove the weak convergence of the average queue length in Proposition 3. We will follow the steps of the proof in Section 7.1 of Braverman et al. (2024).

Using the MGFs $\psi^{{(r)}}$ and $\psi^{{(r)}}_{j}$ of (6.3), we derive an asymptotic BAR for $X^{{(r)}}$ as follows, whose proof depends on SSC and is provided in Section 6.3.

#### Lemma 9.

Assume Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. Under the JSQ or Po2 policy, for each $\eta\leq 0$ , as $r\to 0$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\left(\alpha^{{(r)}}\xi_{e}(r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}})+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mu_{j}\xi_{s,j}(r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}})\right)\psi^{{(r)}}(r\eta) \displaystyle\qquad-\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mu_{j}\mathbb{P}\left(Z_{j}^{{(r)}}=0\right)\xi_{s,j}(r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}})\psi^{{(r)}}_{j}(r\eta)=o(r^{2}), $$

where $f(r)=o(r)$ denotes $\lim_{r\to 0}f(r)/r=0$ .

To rewrite (6.4) in a more tractable form, we need asymptotic expansions of $\xi_{e}$ and $\xi_{s,j}$ for $j\in\mathcal{J}$ . Specifically, for each fixed $\eta\leq 0$ and $j\in\mathcal{J}$ , we have, as $r\to 0$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\xi_{e}(r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}}) \displaystyle=r\eta+\frac{1}{2}c_{e}^{2}r^{2}\eta^{2}+o(r^{2}),\quad\xi_{s,j}(r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}})=-r\eta+\frac{1}{2}c_{s,j}^{2}r^{2}\eta^{2}+o(r^{2}), $$

where $c_{e}^{2}$ and $c_{s,j}^{2}$ are the SCV of interarrival and service times, respectively. The proof of (6.5) is given in Lemma 7.5 of Braverman et al. (2024). Therefore, due to $0\leq\mu_{j}-\lambda_{j}^{{(r)}}\leq r$ in (5.9), the asymptotic BAR (6.4), for each $\eta\leq 0$ , as $r\to 0$ , becomes

$$ \displaystyle\left(r\alpha^{{(r)}}\eta+\frac{1}{2}\alpha^{{(r)}}c_{e}^{2}r^{2}\eta^{2}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(-r\mu_{j}\eta+\frac{1}{2}\mu_{j}c_{s,j}^{2}r^{2}\eta^{2}\right)\right)\psi^{{(r)}}(r\eta) \displaystyle\qquad-\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(\mu_{j}-\lambda^{{(r)}}_{j}\right)\left(-r\eta\right)\psi^{{(r)}}_{j}(r\eta)=o(r^{2}). $$

According to the heavy traffic condition in (2.4) and dividing by $r^{2}\eta$ , we have, for each $\eta\leq 0$ and as $r\to 0$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\left(-1+\eta\left(\frac{1}{2}\alpha^{{(r)}}c_{e}^{2}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{1}{2}\mu_{j}c_{s,j}^{2}\right)\right)\psi^{{(r)}}(r\eta)+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{\mu_{j}-\lambda^{{(r)}}_{j}}{r}\psi^{{(r)}}_{j}(r\eta)=o(1). $$

Using the SSC in Proposition 2 and the expansions in (6.5), we have, as $r\to 0$ ,

$$ \psi^{{(r)}}(r\eta)-\phi^{{(r)}}(r\eta)=o(1),\quad\psi^{{(r)}}_{j}(r\eta)-\phi_{j}^{{(r)}}(r\eta)=o(1)\quad\text{ for }j\in\mathcal{J}, $$

whose proof is given in (7.28) of Braverman et al. (2024). Hence, we can replace $\psi^{{(r)}}$ and $\psi^{{(r)}}_{j}$ by $\phi^{{(r)}}$ and $\phi_{j}^{{(r)}}$ in the asymptotic BAR (6.4), which implies that

$$ \left(-1+\eta\left(\frac{1}{2}\alpha^{{(r)}}c_{e}^{2}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{1}{2}\mu_{j}c_{s,j}^{2}\right)\right)\phi^{{(r)}}(r\eta)+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{\mu_{j}-\lambda^{{(r)}}_{j}}{r}\phi_{j}^{{(r)}}(r\eta)=o(1). $$

According to SSC in Proposition 2, we have the following lemma, and the proof is given in 6.3.

#### Lemma 10.

Assume Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. Under the JSQ or Po2 policy, we have

$$ \lim_{r\to 0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{\mu_{j}-\lambda^{{(r)}}_{j}}{r}\phi_{j}^{{(r)}}(r\eta)=1. $$

Hence, the limit of $\phi^{{(r)}}(r\eta)$ is

$$ \lim_{r\to 0}\phi^{{(r)}}(r\eta)=\frac{1}{1-\eta\left(\frac{1}{2}\alpha^{{(r)}}c_{e}^{2}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{1}{2}\mu_{j}c_{s,j}^{2}\right)}=\frac{1}{1-\eta Jm}, $$

which is the MGF of an exponential random variable with mean $Jm$ , and $m$ is defined in (3.1).

### 6.3 Proof of Technical Lemmas

#### Proof of Lemma 9.

Setting $\theta$ to $r\eta$ , the BAR (6.2) implies that

$$ \displaystyle\left(\alpha^{{(r)}}\xi_{e}(r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}})+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mu_{j}\xi_{s,j}(r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}})\right)\psi^{{(r)}}(r\eta)-\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mu_{j}\mathbb{P}\left(Z_{j}^{{(r)}}=0\right)\xi_{s,j}(r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}})\psi^{{(r)}}_{j}(r\eta) \displaystyle\quad+\alpha^{{(r)}}\xi_{e}(r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}})\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[f_{r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}}}(X^{{(r)}})\mathbbm{1}{\left(\alpha^{{(r)}}R_{e}^{{(r)}}>r^{\varepsilon_{0}-1}\right)}\right] \displaystyle\quad+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mu_{j}\xi_{s,j}(r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}})\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[f_{r\eta,r^{1-\varepsilon_{0}}}(X^{{(r)}})\mathbbm{1}{\left(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}>0\right)}\mathbbm{1}{\left(\mu_{j}R^{{(r)}}_{s,j}>r^{\varepsilon_{0}-1}\right)}\right]=0. $$

Since the last two terms have the order of $o(r^{2})$ by Lemma 8.2 of Braverman et al. (2024), the proof is completed. ∎

#### Proof of Lemma 10.

From the SSC in Proposition 2 and $\mathbb{P}(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0)=(\mu_{j}-\lambda^{{(r)}}_{j})/\mu_{j}$ in (5.9), for each $j\in\mathcal{J}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\left\lvert 1-\phi_{j}^{{(r)}}(r\eta)\right\rvert \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[1-e^{r\eta\sum_{k\in\mathcal{J}}Z^{{(r)}}_{k}}\mid Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right]\leq r\left\lvert\eta\right\rvert\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\sum_{k\in\mathcal{J}}Z^{{(r)}}_{k}\mid Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right] \displaystyle=Jr\left\lvert\eta\right\rvert\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\bar{Z}^{{(r)}}-Z^{{(r)}}_{j}\mid Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right]\leq Jr\left\lvert\eta\right\rvert\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert\mid Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right], $$

where the first inequality follows from $1-e^{-x}\leq x$ for all $x\geq 0$ . By $\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}(\mu_{j}-\lambda_{j}^{{(r)}})=r$ and $\mathbb{P}(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0)=(\mu_{j}-\lambda^{{(r)}}_{j})/\mu_{j}$ in (5.9), we have

$$ \displaystyle\left\lvert 1-\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{\mu_{j}-\lambda^{{(r)}}_{j}}{r}\phi_{j}^{{(r)}}(r\eta)\right\rvert=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{\mu_{j}-\lambda^{{(r)}}_{j}}{r}\left\lvert 1-\phi_{j}^{{(r)}}(r\eta)\right\rvert=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{\mu_{j}\mathbb{P}\left(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right)}{r}\left\lvert 1-\phi_{j}^{{(r)}}(r\eta)\right\rvert \displaystyle\leq\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{\mu_{j}\mathbb{P}\left(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right)}{r}Jr\left\lvert\eta\right\rvert\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert\mid Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right]=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mu_{j}J\left\lvert\eta\right\rvert\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert\mathbbm{1}{\left(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right)}\right] \displaystyle\leq\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mu_{j}J\left\lvert\eta\right\rvert\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{1+\varepsilon_{0}}\right]^{\frac{1}{1+\varepsilon_{0}}}\mathbb{P}\left(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0\right)^{\frac{\varepsilon_{0}}{1+\varepsilon_{0}}}\leq\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mu_{j}^{\frac{1}{1+\varepsilon_{0}}}J\left\lvert\eta\right\rvert\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\lVert Z_{\perp}^{{(r)}}\rVert^{1+\varepsilon_{0}}\right]^{\frac{1}{1+\varepsilon_{0}}}r^{\frac{\varepsilon_{0}}{1+\varepsilon_{0}}} \displaystyle=o(1), $$

where the second inequality holds due to Hölder’s inequality and the final inequality follows from $\mathbb{P}(Z^{{(r)}}_{j}=0)=(\mu_{j}-\lambda^{{(r)}}_{j})/\mu_{j}\leq r/\mu_{j}$ in (5.9). ∎

## Appendix A Proof of Lemma 6

In this section, we provide the proofs of Lemma 6, which is key to the proof of the induction hypotheses (S1)-(S4). We will first prove the JSQ case and then extend the proof to the Po2 case.

Our proof highly depends on the mean value theorem. For any $z\in\mathbb{R}^{J}$ , the gradient of $\lVert z\rVert^{n}$ is given by

$$ \nabla\lVert z\rVert=\frac{z}{\lVert z\rVert},\quad\nabla\lVert z\rVert^{n}=n\lVert z\rVert^{n-2}z. $$

Hence, the mean value theorem implies that for any $z\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}^{J}$ and $\delta\in\mathbb{R}^{J}$ with $\lVert\delta\rVert<1$ , there exists $\xi\in(0,1)$ such that

$$ \lVert z_{\perp}+\delta\rVert^{n}-\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n}=n\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi\delta\rVert^{n-2}\left(z_{\perp}+\xi\delta\right)^{\prime}\delta=\Theta(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-2})\Theta(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert)=\Theta(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}), $$

where $z_{\perp}^{\prime}\delta=\Theta(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert)$ holds due to $\left\lvert z_{\perp}^{\prime}\delta\right\rvert\leq\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert\lVert\delta\rVert$ .

#### JSQ Policy

Since the JSQ policy selects the queue with the shortest job, we have $z_{j}p_{j\mid z}=z_{\min}p_{j\mid z}$ . Hence, (5.11) can be proved as follows. The mean value theorem implies that there exists $\xi_{e,j}\in(0,1)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}+\delta_{j}\rVert^{n+1}p_{j\mid z}-\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n+1}-\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}z_{\perp,\min} \displaystyle\quad=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}+\delta_{j}\rVert^{n+1}-\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n+1}\right)p_{j\mid z}-\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}z_{\perp,\min} \displaystyle\quad=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}\left(z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\right)^{\prime}\delta_{j}p_{j\mid z}-\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}z_{\perp,\min} \displaystyle\quad=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}\left(z_{\perp,\min}+\xi_{e,j}\lVert\delta_{j}\rVert^{2}\right)p_{j\mid z}-\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}z_{\perp,\min} \displaystyle\quad=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}-\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\right)z_{\perp,\min}p_{j\mid z}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}\xi_{e,j}\lVert\delta_{j}\rVert^{2}p_{j\mid z} \displaystyle\quad=O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-2})O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert)+O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1})=O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}), $$

where the third equality follows from the fact that $z_{\perp}^{\prime}\delta_{j}=z_{\perp}^{\prime}e^{{(j)}}=z_{\perp,j}$ and $z_{\perp,j}p_{j\mid z}=z_{\perp,\min}p_{j\mid z}$ , and the fifth equality holds due to (A.1) and $z_{\perp,\min}\leq\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert$ . The proof of (5.12) is similar but more simpler. The mean value theorem implies that there exists $\xi_{s,j}\in(0,1)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}-\delta_{j}\rVert^{n+1}-\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n+1}+\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}z_{\perp,j} \displaystyle\quad=\lVert z_{\perp}-\xi_{s,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}\left(z_{\perp}-\xi_{s,j}\delta_{j}\right)^{\prime}\left(-\delta_{j}\right)+\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}z_{\perp,j} \displaystyle\quad=\lVert z_{\perp}-\xi_{s,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}\xi_{s,j}\lVert\delta_{j}\rVert^{2}-\lVert z_{\perp}-\xi_{s,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}z_{\perp,j}+\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}z_{\perp,j} \displaystyle\quad=O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1})+O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-2})O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert)=O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}), $$

where the second equality follows from the fact that $z_{\perp}^{\prime}\delta_{j}=z_{\perp}^{\prime}e^{{(j)}}=z_{\perp,j}$ , and the third equality holds due to (A.1) and $z_{\perp,j}\leq\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert$ .

The conclusions of (5.13) and (5.14) are the direct consequence of (A.1), so we omit the proof here. Now, we are ready to prove (5.15). Since $\alpha^{{(r)}}=\mu_{\Sigma}-r$ in (2.4), we have

$$ \displaystyle-\mathcal{A}f_{n}(x) \displaystyle=-\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp})\alpha^{{(r)}}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{\perp})\geq-\left(\mu_{\Sigma}-r\right)\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\left(z_{\min}-\bar{z}\right)+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\left(z_{j}-\bar{z}\right)\mu_{j} \displaystyle=\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\left(-r\left(\bar{z}-z_{\min}\right)-\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\mu_{j}\left(z_{\min}-\bar{z}\right)+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(z_{j}-\bar{z}\right)\mu_{j}\right) \displaystyle=\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\left(-r\left(\bar{z}-z_{\min}\right)+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(z_{j}-z_{\min}\right)\mu_{j}\right) \displaystyle\geq\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\left(-r\left(z_{\max}-z_{\min}\right)+\left(z_{\max}-z_{\min}\right)\mu_{\operatorname{argmax}_{k\in\mathcal{J}}z_{k}}\right) \displaystyle=\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\left(\mu_{\min}-r\right)\left({z}_{\max}-z_{\min}\right)\geq\frac{\mu_{\min}}{2\sqrt{J}}\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert^{n}, $$

where the first equality follows from the fact that

$$ z_{\perp,j}\mathbbm{1}{\left(z_{j}>0\right)}=\left(z_{j}-\bar{z}\right)\mathbbm{1}{\left(z_{j}>0\right)}\geq\left(z_{j}-\bar{z}\right)=z_{\perp,j}, $$

the second inequality holds by $z_{\max}\equiv\max_{j\in\mathcal{J}}z_{j}\geq\bar{z}$ and neglecting all terms except the term $z_{\max}$ , and the last inequality holds due to $r\in(0,r_{0})$ with $r_{0}\equiv\mu_{\min}/2$ for JSQ policy and

$$ \left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert=\sqrt{\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(z_{j}-\bar{z}\right)^{2}}\leq\sqrt{\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(z_{\max}-z_{\min}\right)^{2}}=\sqrt{J}\left(z_{\max}-z_{\min}\right). $$

Hence, (5.15) holds for JSQ policy with $b=\mu_{\min}/2\sqrt{J}$ .

#### Po2 Policy

Under the Po2 policy, the decision first selects two stations, $j_{1}$ and $j_{2}$ with probability $p_{j_{1}j_{2}}$ , and then routes the external arrival to the station with the minimum queue length $\operatorname{argmin}_{j\in\{j_{1},j_{2}\}}z_{j}$ . Therefore, we have

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}z_{\perp,j}p_{j|z}=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}z_{j}p_{j|z}-\bar{z}=\sum_{j_{1}<j_{2}}\min\{z_{j_{1}},z_{j_{2}}\}p_{j_{1}j_{2}}-\bar{z}. $$

Applying $\min\{z_{\min},z_{\max}\}=(z_{\min}+z_{\max})/2-(z_{\max}-z_{\min})/2$ for the minimum and maximum queue lengths and $\min\{z_{j_{1}},z_{j_{2}}\}\leq(z_{j_{1}}+z_{j_{2}})/2$ for all other $j_{1},j_{2}\in\mathcal{J}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}z_{\perp,j}p_{j|z} \displaystyle\leq\sum_{j_{1}<j_{2}}\frac{p_{j_{1}j_{2}}}{2}(z_{j_{1}}+z_{j_{2}})-\frac{\min_{j_{1},j_{2}\in\mathcal{J}}p_{j_{1}j_{2}}}{2}(z_{\max}-z_{\min})-\bar{z} \displaystyle=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}{p_{j}}z_{j}-\frac{\min_{j_{1},j_{2}\in\mathcal{J}}p_{j_{1}j_{2}}}{2}(z_{\max}-z_{\min})-\bar{z}\leq\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}{p_{j}}z_{\perp,j}-\frac{p_{\min}^{2}}{\sqrt{J}}\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert, $$

where the last inequality follows from $\min_{j_{1},j_{2}\in\mathcal{J}}p_{j_{1}j_{2}}\leq 2p_{\min}^{2}$ and (A.3). Note that the choice of $\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp})$ is decided by (A.4).

The mean value theorem implies that there exists $\xi_{e,j}\in(0,1)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}+\delta_{j}\rVert^{n+1}p_{j\mid z}-\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n+1}-\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp}) \displaystyle\quad=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}+\delta_{j}\rVert^{n+1}-\frac{1}{n+1}\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n+1}\right)p_{j\mid z}-\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp}) \displaystyle\quad=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}\left(z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\right)^{\prime}\delta_{j}p_{j\mid z}-\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp}) \displaystyle\quad=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}\xi_{e,j}\lVert\delta_{j}\rVert^{2}p_{j\mid z}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}z_{\perp,j}p_{j\mid z}-\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp}) \displaystyle\quad=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}\xi_{e,j}\lVert\delta_{j}\rVert^{2}p_{j\mid z}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}-\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\right)z_{\perp,j}p_{j\mid z} \displaystyle\qquad+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}z_{\perp,j}p_{j\mid z}-\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp}) \displaystyle\quad\leq\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}\xi_{e,j}\lVert\delta_{j}\rVert^{2}p_{j\mid z}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\left(\lVert z_{\perp}+\xi_{e,j}\delta_{j}\rVert^{n-1}-\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\right)z_{\perp,j}p_{j\mid z} \displaystyle\quad=O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1})+O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-2})O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert)=O(\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}), $$

where the third equality follows from the fact that $z_{\perp}^{\prime}\delta_{j}=z_{\perp}^{\prime}e^{{(j)}}=z_{\perp,j}$ , the inequality holds by (A.4), and the fifth equality holds due to (A.1) and $z_{\perp,\min}\leq\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert$ .

The proofs of (5.12), (5.13) and (5.14) are the same as the JSQ case, so we omit them here. Now, we are ready to prove (5.15) for the Po2 policy. Since $\alpha^{{(r)}}=\mu_{\Sigma}-r$ in (2.4), we have

$$ \displaystyle-\mathcal{A}f_{n}(x) \displaystyle=-\eta_{n,e}(z_{\perp})\cdot\alpha^{{(r)}}+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\eta_{n,s,j}(z_{\perp}) \displaystyle\geq-\left(\mu_{\Sigma}-r\right)\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\left(\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}{p_{j}}z_{\perp,j}-\frac{p_{\min}^{2}}{\sqrt{J}}\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert\right)+\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}z_{\perp,j}\mu_{j} \displaystyle=\left(\mu_{\Sigma}-r\right)\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\cdot\frac{p_{\min}^{2}}{\sqrt{J}}\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert-\left(\mu_{\Sigma}-r\right)\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}{p_{j}}z_{\perp,j}+\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}z_{\perp,j}\mu_{j} \displaystyle=\left(\mu_{\Sigma}-r\right)\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\cdot\frac{p_{\min}^{2}}{\sqrt{J}}\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert+r\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}{p_{j}}z_{\perp,j} \displaystyle\geq\left(\mu_{\Sigma}-r\right)\frac{p_{\min}^{2}}{\sqrt{J}}\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert^{n}-r\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert^{n}=\left(\mu_{\Sigma}-\left(1+\frac{\sqrt{J}}{p_{\min}^{2}}\right)r\right)\frac{p_{\min}^{2}}{\sqrt{J}}\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert \displaystyle\geq\frac{\mu_{\Sigma}}{2}\frac{p_{\min}^{2}}{\sqrt{J}}\left\lVert z_{\perp}\right\rVert^{n}, $$

where the first inequality holds due to (A.2), the third equality follows from the fact that $p_{j}=\mu_{j}/\mu_{\Sigma}$ , the second inequality holds by $z_{\perp,j}\geq-\lVert z_{\perp}\rVert$ , and the last inequality holds due to $r\in(0,r_{0})$ where $r_{0}\leq\mu_{\Sigma}/(1+\frac{p_{\min}^{2}}{\sqrt{J}})$ for Po2 policy. Hence, (5.15) holds for Po2 policy with $b=\mu_{\Sigma}p_{\min}^{2}/(2\sqrt{J})$ and the proof of Lemma 6 is completed.
