#### 7.0.0.2 Yeast cross dataset

The yeast cross dataset55 5 The dataset is downloaded from http://genomics-pubs.princeton.edu/YeastCross_BYxRM/home.shtml. consists of 1,008 prototrophic haploid segregants from a cross between a laboratory strain and a wine strain of yeast. This dataset was collected via high-coverage sequencing and consists of genotypes at 30,594 high-confidence single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that distinguish the strains and densely cover the genome. There are 46 traits in this dataset corresponding to the measured growth under multiple conditions, including different temperatures, pHs and carbon sources, as well as addition of metal ions and small molecules [12]. The goal is to study the relationship between genotypes and traits, which could be used for predicting traits or selecting significant genotypes for further scientific investigation [12]. A multivariate linear regression by regressing traits on genotypes could be suitable for this purpose. However, it is likely that there exist hidden factors that also affect traits. We thus fit our model (1.4) for prediction and variable selection. After removing the segregants with missing values in traits and SNPs which have Pearson correlations above $0.97$ , we end up with $n=303$ segregants with $m=46$ traits and $p=571$ SNPs.

To evaluate the prediction performance, we randomly split the data into $70\%$ training set and $30\%$ test set. We center and normalize the SNPs in the training set to zero mean and unit variance. Traits in the training set are also centered. The corresponding means and scales from the training set are used to standardize the test set. We then apply the HIVE Algorithm 1 together with group-lasso (Lasso) and Ridge to the training set and evaluate the fitted model on the test set. The test mean square errors (MSE) of Lasso and Ridge are 7.29 and 6.29, respectively, while HIVE has a smaller test MSE 5.92. This suggests that HIVE has better prediction performance than Lasso and Ridge. We then refit the model to the whole dataset and apply HIVE, H-HIVE and Lasso for variable selection. Lasso and HIVE select, respectively, 261 and 259 SNPs with 205 common ones. For H-HIVE, it selects 263 SNPs in which 222 SNPs are identical to those selected from Lasso. The difference of the selected SNPs between HIVE (H-HIVE) and Lasso is due to the fact that Lasso does not account for the potential hidden variables. We expect that the results from HIVE (H-HIVE) may provide new insight on understanding how SNPs are associated with different traits. For instance, further confirmatory analysis such as controlled experiments can be conducted by the investigators to study the effect of the selected SNPs.

## 8 Discussion

In this paper, we study the high-dimensional multivariate response regression model with hidden variables. We establish sufficient and necessary conditions for model identifiability. We propose the HIVE algorithm for estimating the coefficient matrix $\Theta^{*}$ , which is adaptive to the unknown sparsity of $\Theta^{*}$ . The algorithm is further extended to settings with heteroscedastic noise. Theoretically, we establish non-asymptotic upper bounds of the estimation error of our estimator, which are valid for any finite $n$ , $p$ , $m$ and $K$ .

There are several future directions that are worthy of further investigation. First, it is appealing to study the variable selection property of the proposed algorithm. In this paper, we focus on the adaptive estimation of the coefficient matrix. To establish the variable selection consistency property, a different set of conditions (e.g., minimum signal strength condition) are required. Second, it is of great interest to construct confidence intervals or hypothesis tests for the high-dimensional matrix $\Theta^{*}$ [34]. The inference results can be further used to control the false discovery rate (FDR) in multiple testing, which is of central importance in many biological applications. We refer to the SVA literature for discussions on the FDR control. Third, our model (1.1) also covers a particular yet important model, the confounding model [22], which, in addition to (1.1), assumes $X=D^{\prime}Z+W^{\prime}$ for some random noise $W^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ independent of $Z$ . As a result, the coefficient $\Psi^{*}$ represents the causal effect of $X$ on $Y$ . Both our methods and analysis are directly applicable to this case. But it is also worth mentioning that assuming this extra structure brings the advantage of predicting $Z$ by using $X$ when $p$ is large. The predicted $Z$ in turn could potentially be used to improve the estimation of $\Psi^{*}$ , especially when $m$ is small. We do not pursue this direction in this paper and leave it to future research.

## A A variant of the robust $\sin\Theta$ theorem

We state a variant of Theorem 3 (Robust $\sin\Theta$ theorem) in [60]. Let $N,M$ and $Z$ be $m\times m$ deterministic symmetric matrices satisfying

$$ N=M+Z $$

where $N$ is the observation matrix while $M$ is the matrix of interest with $\textrm{rank}(M)=K$ . Let $V\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times K}$ denote the first $K$ eigenvectors of $M$ with non-increasing eigenvalues denoted as $\lambda_{1}(M)\geq\lambda_{2}(M)\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_{K}(M)$ . Further let $\widehat{V}$ be the output of Algorithm 2 applied to $N$ . Define $\sin\Theta(\widehat{V},V):=\widehat{V}_{\perp}^{T}V$ where $\widehat{V}_{\perp}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times(m-K)}$ is the orthogonal complement of $\widehat{V}$ such that $[\widehat{V},\widehat{V}_{\perp}]$ is the complete orthogonal matrix. The following theorem provides upper bounds for the Frobenius norm of $\sin\Theta(\widehat{V},V)$ . For any matrix $D$ , let $G(D)$ be the matrix with diagonal entries equal to those of $D$ and off-diagonal entries equal to zero. Let $\Gamma(D)=D-G(D)$ .

#### Theorem 13.

Suppose $M\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}$ is a rank- $K$ symmetric matrix and $V$ consists of its first $K$ eigenvectors. Assume there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that

$$ \max_{1\leq j\leq m}\left\|e_{j}^{T}V\right\|_{2}^{2}\cdot{\lambda_{1}(M)\over\lambda_{K}(M)}\leq c $$

and $\|\Gamma(Z)\|_{F}\leq c\sqrt{K}\lambda_{K}(M)$ . Then the output $\widehat{V}$ of HeteroPCA( $N,K,T$ ) in Algorithm 2 with $T=\Omega\bigl(1\vee\log{\sqrt{K}\lambda_{K}(M)\over\|\Gamma(Z)\|_{F}}\bigr)$ satisfies

$$ \|\sin\Theta(\widehat{V},V)\|_{F}~\lesssim~{\|\Gamma(Z)\|_{F}\over\lambda_{K}(M)}\wedge\sqrt{K}. $$

The proof follows the same arguments as that of Theorem 7 (General robust $\sin\Theta$ theorem) in [60] by taking the sparsity set $\mathcal{G}=\{(i,i):1\leq i\leq m\}$ and $b=\eta=1$ . We will use the same notations as [60].

Define $T_{0}=\|\Gamma(N-M)\|_{F}=\|\Gamma(Z)\|_{F}$ and $K_{t}=\|N^{(t)}-M\|_{F}$ for $t=0,1,\ldots,$ . Note that $\|H\|_{F}\leq\|\Gamma(H)\|_{F}+\|G(H)\|_{F}$ for all matrix $H\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}$ . We then revisit the three steps in the proof of Theorem 7 in [60] by only restating the main results and differences from [60]. We use $V$ and $V^{(t)}$ in lieu of $U$ and $U^{(t)}$ in the original proofs of [60] for all $t\geq 0$ .

Step 1: The initial errors satisfy

$$ \displaystyle K_{0} \displaystyle\leq\|\Gamma(Z)\|_{F}+\|G(P_{V}MP_{V})\|_{F} \displaystyle\leq\|\Gamma(Z)\|_{F}+\|M\|_{F}\max_{i}\|e_{i}^{T}V\|_{2} \displaystyle\leq\|\Gamma(Z)\|_{F}+c\sqrt{K}\lambda_{K}(M) $$

for some sufficiently small constant $c>0$ where the first inequality follows from the same arguments in [60], the second inequality uses the modified Lemma 5 and the third inequality uses $\|M\|_{F}\leq\sqrt{K}\|M\|_{op}=\sqrt{K}\lambda_{1}(M)$ together with condition (A.2).

Step 2: From the proof of [60], one needs to upper bound the two terms on the right hand side of the following display

$$ K_{t}\leq\|\Gamma(N^{(t)})-M\|_{F}+\|G(N^{(t)}-M)\|_{F}. $$

The first term satisfies

$$ \|\Gamma(N^{(t)})-M\|_{F}=\|\Gamma(N-M)\|_{F}=T_{0} $$

for all $t\geq 0$ . The second term can be upper bounded by (see display (6.15) in [60])

$$ \displaystyle\|G(N^{(t)}-M)\|_{F} \displaystyle~\leq~\|G(P_{V}(N^{(t-1)}-M))\|_{F}+\|G(P_{V^{(t-1)_{\perp}}}M)\|_{F} \displaystyle\qquad+\|\left(P_{V^{(t-1)}}-P_{V}\right)(N^{(t-1)}-M)\|_{F}. $$

To bound them separately, we have

$$ \displaystyle\|G(P_{V}(N^{(t-1)}-M))\|_{F} \displaystyle~\leq~\|N^{(t-1)}-M\|_{F}\max_{i}\|e_{i}^{T}V\|_{2} \displaystyle~=~K_{t-1}\max_{i}\|e_{i}^{T}V\|_{2} $$

by Lemma 5, and

$$ \displaystyle\|G(P_{V^{(t-1)_{\perp}}}M)\|_{F} \displaystyle~\leq~\|G(P_{V^{(t-1)_{\perp}}}MP_{V})\|_{F} \displaystyle~\leq~\|P_{V^{(t-1)_{\perp}}}M\|_{F}\max_{i}\|e_{i}^{T}V\|_{2} \displaystyle~\leq~2\|N^{(t-1)}-M\|_{F}\max_{i}\|e_{i}^{T}V\|_{2} \displaystyle~=~2K_{t-1}\max_{i}\|e_{i}^{T}V\|_{2} $$

by using Lemma 5 in the second inequality and using Lemma 7 in [60] in the third inequality. Finally, the proof of Theorem 7 in [60] shows that

$$ \displaystyle\|P_{V^{(t-1)}}-P_{V}\|_{op} \displaystyle\leq{4\|N^{(t-1)}-M\|_{op}\over\lambda_{K}(M)}\wedge 1\leq{4K_{t-1}\over\lambda_{K}(M)} $$

which further gives

$$ \|\left(P_{V^{(t-1)}}-P_{V}\right)(N^{(t-1)}-M)\|_{F}\leq\|P_{V^{(t-1)}}-P_{V}\|_{op}\|N^{(t-1)}-M\|_{F}\leq{4K^{2}_{t-1}\over\lambda_{K}(M)}. $$

Collecting (A.3) – (A.6) yields

$$ K_{t}\leq T_{0}+3K_{t-1}\max_{i}\|e_{i}^{T}V\|_{2}+{4K^{2}_{t-1}\over\lambda_{K}(M)} $$

Step 3: Finally, by using the same induction arguments in [60], under (A.2) and $\|\Gamma(Z)\|_{F}=T_{0}\leq c\sqrt{K}\lambda_{K}(M)$ with sufficiently small $c$ , one can show that for all $t\geq 0$ ,

$$ K_{t}\leq 2T_{0}+{\sqrt{K}\lambda_{K}(M)\over 2^{t+4}}. $$

Therefore, for all $t\geq\Omega(1\vee\log({\sqrt{K}\lambda_{K}(M)/T_{0}}))$ , one has $K_{t}\leq 3T_{0}$ . The proof is completed by invoking the variant of Davis-Kahan’s $\sin\Theta$ theorem [57] applied to $N^{(t)}$ and $M$ with $d=s=K$ , $r=1$ and $\lambda_{K+1}(M)=0$ . ∎

The following lemma is a variant of Lemma 1 in [60] and it provides upper bounds for the Frobenius norms of some diagonal matrices. Recall that $G(A)$ has the same diagonal elements with $A$ but all off-diagonal entries equal to zero.

#### Lemma 5.

For any two orthogonal matrices $U,V\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times K}$ , let $P_{U}=UU^{T}$ and $P_{V}=VV^{T}$ . Then for any matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\|G(P_{U}A)\|_{F}^{2}\leq\|A\|_{F}^{2}\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\left\|e_{i}^{T}U\right\|_{2}^{2}, \displaystyle\|G(AP_{V})\|_{F}^{2}\leq\|A\|_{F}^{2}\max_{1\leq j\leq m}\left\|e_{j}^{T}V\right\|_{2}^{2}, \displaystyle\|G(P_{U}AP_{V})\|_{F}^{2}\leq\|A\|_{F}^{2}\left(\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\left\|e_{i}^{T}U\right\|_{2}^{2}\wedge\max_{1\leq j\leq m}\left\|e_{j}^{T}V\right\|_{2}^{2}\right). $$

Since $G(A)$ has non-zero entries only on the diagonal, by writing $A=(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m})$ , one has

$$ \displaystyle\|G(P_{U}A)\|_{F}^{2}=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(e_{i}^{T}UU^{T}A_{i}\right)^{2} \displaystyle\leq\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\|e_{i}^{T}U\|_{2}^{2}\cdot\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_{i}^{T}UU^{T}A_{i} \displaystyle=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\|e_{i}^{T}U\|_{2}^{2}\cdot\textrm{tr}(A^{T}UU^{T}A) \displaystyle\leq\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\|e_{i}^{T}U\|_{2}^{2}\cdot\|A\|_{F}^{2} $$

where we used Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in the first line and the inequality $\textrm{tr}(A^{T}UU^{T}A)\leq\|A\|_{F}^{2}\|UU^{T}\|_{op}\leq\|A\|_{F}^{2}$ in the last line. Since $G(P_{U}A)$ is symmetric to $G(AP_{V})$ , the second result follows. The last result follows by using the first two results together with $\|P_{V}\|_{op}\leq 1$ and $\|P_{U}\|_{op}\leq 1$ . ∎

## B Main proofs

### B.1 Proof of Proposition 1: $\Psi^{*}$ is not identifiable

Under model (1.1), we will show that there exists $\Psi_{1}\neq\Psi_{2}$ such that they yield the same likelihood. For simplicity, we suppress the super script $*$ for related parameters and use lower case letters $x,y,z$ to denote the realizations of random variables $X,Y,Z$ . Since the joint density of $(X,Y)$ is factorized as

$$ \displaystyle f_{(Y,X)}(y,x)=f_{Y|X}(y|x)f_{X}(x)=f_{X}(x)\int f_{Y|X,Z}(y|x,z)f_{Z|X}(z|x)dz, $$

under model (1.1), we can write the likelihood of $(Y,X)$ as

$$ \displaystyle f_{(Y,X)}\left(y,x;\Psi,B,\mu,\nu\right) \displaystyle=f_{X}(x)\int f_{E}\left(y-\Psi^{T}x-B^{T}z;\mu\right)f_{Z|X}(z;\nu)dz $$

where $f_{E}$ denotes the density of $E$ parametrized by $\mu$ and $f_{Z|X}$ is the conditional p.d.f. of $Z=z|X=x$ parametrized by $\nu$ . We emphasize that $\nu=\nu(x)$ depends on $X=x$ as $Z$ is correlated with $X$ as $A^{*}\neq 0$ . For any $\Psi$ such that $\Psi P_{B}\neq 0$ (this choice exists as $\textrm{rank}(B)=K$ ), write

$$ \widetilde{\Psi}=\Psi-\Psi P_{B}=\Psi-\Psi B^{T}(BB^{T})^{-1}B,\qquad\widetilde{Z}=Z+(BB^{T})^{-1}B\Psi^{T}X. $$

Note that $\widetilde{\Psi}\neq\Psi$ as $\Psi P_{B}\neq 0$ . We prove the following to conclude the proof

$$ f_{(Y,X)}\left(y,x;\Psi,B,\mu,\nu\right)=f_{(Y,X)}\left(y,x;\widetilde{\Psi},B,\mu,\widetilde{\nu}\right) $$

where $\widetilde{\nu}$ parametrizes the p.d.f of $\widetilde{Z}|X$ .

To proceed, write $\Delta=\Psi B^{T}(BB^{T})^{-1}$ such that $\widetilde{Z}=Z+\Delta^{T}X$ . Observe that the density functions of $Z|X$ and $\widetilde{Z}|X$ only differ by a shift of the mean. We then deduce

$$ f_{\widetilde{Z}|X}\left(z;\widetilde{\nu}\right)=f_{Z|X}\left(z-\Delta^{T}x;\nu\right), $$

from which we further obtain

$$ \displaystyle f_{(Y,X)}\left(y,x;\widetilde{\Psi},B,\mu,\widetilde{\nu}\right) \displaystyle=f_{X}(x)\int f_{E}\left(y-\widetilde{\Psi}^{T}x-B^{T}z;\mu\right)f_{\widetilde{Z}|X}\left(z;\widetilde{\nu}\right)dz \displaystyle=f_{X}(x)\int f_{E}\left(y-\widetilde{\Psi}^{T}x-B^{T}z;\mu\right)f_{Z|X}\left(z-\Delta^{T}x;\nu\right)dz \displaystyle=f_{X}(x)\int f_{E}\left(y-\widetilde{\Psi}^{T}x-B^{T}t-B^{T}\Delta^{T}x;\mu\right)f_{Z|X}\left(t;\nu\right)dt \displaystyle=f_{X}(x)\int f_{E}\left(y-\Psi^{T}x-B^{T}t;\mu\right)f_{Z|X}\left(t;\nu\right)dt \displaystyle=f_{(Y,X)}\left(y,x;\Psi,B,\mu,\nu\right). $$

We use (B.1) in the first and last equality, set $t=z-\Delta^{T}x$ to derive the third equality and use

$$ \widetilde{\Psi}^{T}x=\Psi^{T}x-B^{T}(BB^{T})^{-1}B\Psi^{T}x=\Psi^{T}x-B^{T}\Delta^{T}x $$

to arrive at the fourth equality. This completes the proof.∎

### B.2 Proofs of Propositions 2 and 9: identifiability for both homoscedastic and heteroscedastic cases

When $\Psi^{*}P_{B^{*}}+A^{*}B^{*}=0$ , the uniqueness of $\Theta^{*}$ follows trivially. We only prove case (2). Model (1.4) implies

$$ F^{*}=\Psi^{*}+A^{*}B^{*}=[\text{Cov}(X)]^{-1}\text{Cov}(X,Y), $$

from which we can identify

$$ \Sigma_{\varepsilon}:=\text{Cov}(\varepsilon)=\text{Cov}(Y-(F^{*})^{T}X). $$

By further using $\Sigma_{E}=\tau^{2}{\bm{I}}_{m}$ , we have

$$ \Sigma_{\varepsilon}=(B^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}+\Sigma_{E}=(B^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}+\tau^{2}{\bm{I}}_{m} $$

Recall that $P_{B^{*}}$ denotes the projection onto the row space of $B^{*}$ . One can identify it from

$$ P_{B^{*}}=U_{K}U_{K}^{T} $$

where $U_{K}$ are the eigenvectors of $\Sigma_{\varepsilon}$ corresponding to the largest $K$ eigenvalues. Projecting $Y$ onto $P_{B^{*}}^{\perp}={\bm{I}}_{m}-P_{B^{*}}$ gives

$$ P_{B^{*}}^{\perp}Y=(\Psi^{*}P_{B^{*}}^{\perp})^{T}X+P_{B^{*}}^{\perp}E=(\Theta^{*})^{T}X+P_{B^{*}}^{\perp}E. $$

We then conclude

$$ \Theta^{*}=[\text{Cov}(X)]^{-1}\text{Cov}(X,P_{B^{*}}^{\perp}Y) $$

which is uniquely defined. ∎

The proof of Proposition 9 uses the same arguments as that of Proposition 2 except the identifiability of $P_{B^{*}}$ , the projection onto the row space of $B^{*}$ . After identifying $\Sigma_{\varepsilon}$ , note that

$$ \Sigma_{\varepsilon}=(B^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}+\textrm{diag}(\tau_{1}^{2},\ldots,\tau_{m}^{2}). $$

Under (4.2), applying Theorem 13 with $N=\Sigma_{\varepsilon}$ , $M=(B^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}$ , $Z=\textrm{diag}(\tau_{1}^{2},\ldots,\tau_{m}^{2})$ and $T\to\infty$ identifies $P_{B^{*}}$ . Hence the identifiability of $\Theta^{*}$ follows from the same arguments in the previous proof. ∎

### Proof of Proposition 3: the necessity of $\textrm{rank}(\Sigma_{W})=K$

We drop the superscripts $*$ for simplicity. Under model

$$ Y=(\Theta+\Psi P_{B}+AB)^{T}X+B^{T}W+E, $$

with $\Theta=\Psi P_{B}^{\perp}$ , suppose $\mathbb{E}[W|X]=0$ and $\Psi P_{B}+AB\neq 0$ . We will show that $\Theta$ is not identifiable if $\textrm{rank}(\Sigma_{W})<K$ . Towards this end, we shall construct $(\Psi,A,B)\neq(\widetilde{\Psi},A,\widetilde{B})$ such that

$$ \widetilde{\Psi}+A\widetilde{B}=\Psi+AB,\quad\widetilde{B}^{T}W=B^{T}W,\text{ a.s.} $$

meanwhile

$$ \widetilde{\Psi}P_{\widetilde{B}}+A\widetilde{B}\neq 0,\quad\widetilde{\Theta}=\widetilde{\Psi}P_{\widetilde{B}}^{\perp}\neq\Psi P_{B}^{\perp}=\Theta. $$

Suppose $\textrm{rank}(\Sigma_{W})<K$ . Then there exists a subspace $\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{K}$ with $\textrm{rank}(\mathcal{S})=K-\textrm{rank}(\Sigma_{W})$ such that

$$ v^{T}\Sigma_{W}v=0,\qquad\text{for any }v\in\mathcal{S}. $$

Let $P_{\mathcal{S}}\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times K}$ denote the projection matrix onto $\mathcal{S}$ and $P_{\mathcal{S}}^{\perp}={\bm{I}}_{K}-P_{\mathcal{S}}$ .

Write

$$ \widetilde{B}=P_{\mathcal{S}}^{\perp}B=B-P_{\mathcal{S}}B,\qquad\widetilde{\Psi}=\Psi+AP_{\mathcal{S}}B. $$

Note that (B.3) implies $\widetilde{B}^{T}W=B^{T}W$ a.s. and

$$ \widetilde{\Psi}+A\widetilde{B}=\Psi+AP_{\mathcal{S}}B+AP_{\mathcal{S}}^{\perp}B=\Psi+AB. $$

It remains to show (B.2). We choose $\Psi$ such that $\Psi P_{B}=0$ which also implies $\Psi P_{\widetilde{B}}=0$ and $AB\neq 0$ from the constraint $\Psi P_{B}+AB\neq 0$ . Then

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{\Psi}P_{\widetilde{B}}+A\widetilde{B} \displaystyle=\Psi P_{\widetilde{B}}+AP_{\mathcal{S}}BP_{\widetilde{B}}+A\widetilde{B} \displaystyle=AP_{\mathcal{S}}BP_{\widetilde{B}}+A\widetilde{B}P_{\widetilde{B}} \displaystyle=ABP_{\widetilde{B}}. $$

Furthermore, $\Psi P_{B}=\Psi P_{\widetilde{B}}=0$ gives

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{\Psi}P_{\widetilde{B}}^{\perp}-\Psi P_{B}^{\perp} \displaystyle=\left(\Psi+AP_{\mathcal{S}}B\right)P_{\widetilde{B}}^{\perp}-\Psi=AP_{\mathcal{S}}BP_{\widetilde{B}}^{\perp}=ABP_{\widetilde{B}}^{\perp}. $$

Since there exists various choices of $A$ such that $ABP_{\widetilde{B}}\neq 0$ and $ABP_{\widetilde{B}}^{\perp}\neq 0$ (for instance, any $A$ with $\textrm{rank}(A)=K$ suffices), this concludes that $\Theta^{*}$ is not identifiable, hence completes the proof. ∎

### B.3 Proof of Theorem 4: in-sample prediction risk

Before proving Theorem 4, we first prove Lemma 1 as it provides a simpler analytical expression for the later proof.

From (2.3), for any fixed $\Psi$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\widehat{L}(\Psi) \displaystyle=\arg\min_{L}{1\over n}\|{\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi-{\bm{X}}L\|_{F}^{2}+\lambda_{2}\|L\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle=({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi). $$

Plugging this into (2.3) yields

$$ \displaystyle\widehat{\Psi} \displaystyle=\arg\min_{\Psi}{1\over n}\|{\bm{Y}}-P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{Y}}+P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}\Psi-{\bm{X}}\Psi\|_{F}^{2}+\lambda_{1}\|\Psi\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+\lambda_{2}\|\widehat{L}(\Psi)\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle=\arg\min_{\Psi}{1\over n}\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi)\|_{F}^{2}+\lambda_{1}\|\Psi\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}} \displaystyle\hskip 56.9055pt+\lambda_{2}\|({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi)\|_{F}^{2}. $$

Since

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi)\|_{F}^{2}+\lambda_{2}\|({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi)\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle=\textrm{tr}\left\{({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi)^{T}\left[{1\over n}Q_{\lambda_{2}}^{2}+\lambda_{2}{\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-2}{\bm{X}}^{T}\right]({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi)\right\} $$

and

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}Q_{\lambda_{2}}^{2}+\lambda_{2}{\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-2}{\bm{X}}^{T} \displaystyle={1\over n}\biggl[{\bm{I}}_{p}+{\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T} \displaystyle\qquad-2{\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-2}{\bm{X}}^{T}\biggr] \displaystyle={1\over n}\biggl[{\bm{I}}_{p}-{\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}\biggr] \displaystyle={1\over n}Q_{\lambda_{2}} $$

by using $n\lambda_{2}{\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-2}{\bm{X}}^{T}={\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}(n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}$ in the last line, we obtain

$$ \widehat{\Psi}=\arg\min_{\Psi}{1\over n}\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}^{1/2}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi)\|_{F}^{2}+\lambda_{1}\|\Psi\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}. $$

This proves (2.5). As a result, we have

$$ {\bm{X}}\widehat{L}(\widehat{\Psi})={\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\widehat{\Psi})=P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{Y}}-P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}\widehat{\Psi} $$

hence

$$ {\bm{X}}\widehat{F}={\bm{X}}\widehat{L}(\widehat{\Psi})+{\bm{X}}\widehat{\Psi}=P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{Y}}+Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}\widehat{\Psi}. $$

The proof is complete. ∎

To prove Theorem 4, recall that, for any $(\Psi_{0},L_{0})$ such that $F^{*}=\Psi_{0}+L_{0}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle{\bm{X}}\widehat{F}-{\bm{X}}F^{*} \displaystyle={\bm{X}}\widehat{L}-{\bm{X}}L_{0}+{\bm{X}}\widehat{\Psi}-{\bm{X}}\Psi_{0} \displaystyle=P_{\lambda_{2}}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi_{0})-{\bm{X}}L_{0}+Q_{\lambda_{2}}({\bm{X}}\widehat{\Psi}-{\bm{X}}\Psi_{0}). $$

The result of Theorem 4 follows by invoking Lemmas 6 – 7 and noting that

$$ {1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}\widehat{F}-{\bm{X}}F^{*}\|_{F}^{2}\leq{2\over n}\|P_{\lambda_{2}}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi_{0})-{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}^{2}+{2\over n}\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}({\bm{X}}\widehat{\Psi}-{\bm{X}}\Psi_{0})\|_{F}^{2} $$

from the basic inequality $(a+b)^{2}\leq 2(a^{2}+b^{2})$ . We then proceed to upper bound the two terms on the right hand side separately.

#### Lemma 6.

Under conditions in Theorem 4, with probability $1-\epsilon$ ,

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|P_{\lambda_{2}}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi_{0})-{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle\leq 2\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\cdot\lambda_{2}{\rm tr}\left[L_{0}^{T}\widehat{\Sigma}(\widehat{\Sigma}+\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}L_{0}\right] \displaystyle\quad+{2V_{\varepsilon}\over n}\left[\sqrt{{\rm tr}(P_{\lambda_{2}}^{2})}+\sqrt{2\|P_{\lambda_{2}}^{2}\|_{op}\log(m/\epsilon)}\right]^{2} $$

where $V_{\varepsilon}$ is defined in (3.3).

By ${\bm{Y}}={\bm{X}}\Psi_{0}+{\bm{X}}L_{0}+{\bm{\varepsilon}}$ and the basic inequality $(a+b)^{2}\leq 2(a^{2}+b^{2})$ , we have

$$ \|P_{\lambda_{2}}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi_{0})-{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}^{2}\leq 2\|P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{F}^{2}+2\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}^{2}. $$

Note that the second term satisfies

$$ \displaystyle\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}^{2}\leq\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}^{1/2}{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}^{2}=\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\cdot n\lambda_{2}\textrm{tr}\left[L_{0}^{T}\widehat{\Sigma}(\widehat{\Sigma}+\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}L_{0}\right] $$

by using Fact 1 in the second equality. The result follows by invoking Lemma 14 for the term $\|P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{F}^{2}$ . ∎

#### Lemma 7.

Under conditions in Theorem 4, with probability $1-\epsilon^{\prime}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0})\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle\leq 4\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\cdot\max\left\{4\lambda_{2}{\rm tr}\left[L_{0}^{T}\widehat{\Sigma}(\widehat{\Sigma}+\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}L_{0}\right],~{\lambda_{1}^{2}\over[\kappa_{1}(1/2,\Psi_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}]^{2}}\right\} $$

Write $\widetilde{\bm{Y}}=Q_{\lambda_{2}}^{1/2}{\bm{Y}}$ and $\widetilde{\bm{X}}=Q_{\lambda_{2}}^{1/2}{\bm{X}}$ . Starting with (2.5), we have

$$ {1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{Y}}-\widetilde{\bm{X}}\widehat{\Psi}\|_{F}^{2}+\lambda_{1}\|\widehat{\Psi}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\leq{1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{Y}}-\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Psi_{0}\|_{F}^{2}+\lambda_{1}\|\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}. $$

Let $\langle A,B\rangle=\textrm{tr}(A^{T}B)$ for any commensurate matrices $A$ and $B$ . By writing $\Delta:=\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0}$ and noting that $\widetilde{\bm{Y}}=\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Psi_{0}+\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}+\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}}$ with $\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}}=Q_{\lambda_{2}}^{1/2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}$ , standard arguments yield

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle\leq{2\over n}\left|\langle\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}+\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}},\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\rangle\right|+\lambda_{1}\left(\|\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\widehat{\Psi}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right) \displaystyle\leq{2\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}+{2\over n}\left|\langle\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}},\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\rangle\right|+\lambda_{1}\left(\|\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Delta+\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right) \displaystyle\leq{2\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}+{2\over n}\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+\lambda_{1}\left(\|\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Delta+\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right) $$

where we use Cauchy-Schwarz in the second inequality and the following display to derive the third inequality,

$$ \left|\langle\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}},\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\rangle\right|=\left|\sum_{j=1}^{p}\widetilde{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}}\Delta_{j\cdot}\right|\leq\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}. $$

On the event

$$ \mathcal{E}:=\left\{\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}\leq{n\over 4}\cdot\lambda_{1}\right\}, $$

by $\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}=\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}$ , we further have

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2}\left(1-{2\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}\over\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}}\right)\leq\lambda_{1}\left(\|\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Delta+\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+{1\over 2}\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right) $$

Notice that

$$ \|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}^{2}=\textrm{tr}\left[L_{0}^{T}{\bm{X}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L_{0}\right]=n\lambda_{2}\textrm{tr}\left[L_{0}^{T}\widehat{\Sigma}(\widehat{\Sigma}+\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}L_{0}\right] $$

by using Fact 1. When $\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}\leq 4\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}$ , we obtain the desired result from (B.9). It suffices to consider the case $\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}\geq 4\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}$ . Display (B.8) then implies

$$ {1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2}\leq 2\lambda_{1}\left(\|\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Delta+\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+{1\over 2}\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right), $$

from which we conclude $\Delta\in\mathcal{R}(1/2,\Psi_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})$ defined in (3.2). Invoking condition (3.1) with $c=1$ gives

$$ {1\over\sqrt{n}}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}\leq{2\lambda_{1}\over\kappa_{1}(1/2,\Psi_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})}. $$

Therefore, on the event $\mathcal{E}$ , by combining with (B.9), we have

$$ {1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2}\leq\max\left\{16\lambda_{2}\textrm{tr}\left[L_{0}^{T}\widehat{\Sigma}(\widehat{\Sigma}+\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}L_{0}\right],{4\lambda_{1}^{2}\over\kappa_{1}^{2}(1/2,\Psi_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})}\right\}. $$

Since the choice of $\lambda_{1}$ in (3.4) together with Lemma 15 implies $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E})=1-\epsilon^{\prime}$ , we conclude the proof by invoking (3.4) in the above display. ∎

### B.4 Proof of Theorem 6: convergence rate of $\|\widetilde{\Theta}-\Theta^{*}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}$

We work on the event $\mathcal{E}_{B^{*}}:=\{\|\widehat{P}-P_{B^{*}}\|_{F}\leq c\xi_{n}\}$ for some constant $c>0$ . Define

$$ Rem_{5}=C\left\{{1\over\sqrt{n}}\|{\bm{X}}F^{*}\|_{op}+\Lambda_{1}^{1/2}\left(1+\sqrt{K\over n}\right)\right\}\xi_{n} $$

for some constant $C>0$ . We will prove that for any $\lambda_{3}\geq\bar{\lambda}_{3}$ , the solution $\widetilde{\Theta}$ from (2.8) satisfies

$$ \displaystyle{1\over\sqrt{n}}\|{\bm{X}}\widetilde{\Theta}-{\bm{X}}\Theta^{*}\|_{F}\leq\max\left\{4Rem_{5},~{3\lambda_{3}\sqrt{s_{*}}\over\kappa(s_{*},3)}\right\}, \displaystyle\|\widetilde{\Theta}-\Theta^{*}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\lesssim\max\left\{{Rem_{5}^{2}\over\lambda_{3}},~{\lambda_{3}s_{*}\over\kappa^{2}(s_{*},4)}\right\} $$

with probability $1-\varepsilon-2e^{-c^{\prime\prime}K}$ for some constant $c^{\prime\prime}>0$ . Then the result of Theorem 6 follows immediately by noting that $Rem_{5}=\widetilde{\lambda}_{3}\sqrt{s_{*}}/\kappa(s_{*},4)$ .

We proceed to prove (B.12) and (B.13). Pick any $\lambda_{3}\geq\bar{\lambda}_{3}$ . Starting from (2.5), by writing $\Delta:=\widetilde{\Theta}-\Theta^{*}$ , standard arguments yield

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle\leq{2\over n}\left|\langle{\bm{Y}}\widehat{P}^{\perp}-{\bm{X}}\Theta^{*},{\bm{X}}\Delta\rangle\right|+\lambda_{3}\left(\|\Theta^{*}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\widetilde{\Theta}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right) \displaystyle\leq{2\over n}\left|\langle{\bm{E}}\widehat{P}^{\perp},{\bm{X}}\Delta\rangle\right|+{2\over n}\left|\langle({\bm{X}}F^{*}+{\bm{W}}B^{*})\widehat{P}^{\perp}-{\bm{X}}\Theta^{*},{\bm{X}}\Delta\rangle\right| \displaystyle\qquad+\lambda_{3}\left(\|\Delta_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Delta_{S_{*}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right) $$

with $S_{*}:=\{1\leq j\leq p:\|\Theta^{*}_{j\cdot}\|_{2}\neq 0\}$ . Since

$$ \left|\langle{\bm{E}}\widehat{P}^{\perp},{\bm{X}}\Delta\rangle\right|\leq\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}{\bm{E}}\widehat{P}^{\perp}\|_{2}, $$

on the event $\mathcal{E}^{\prime}$ defined as

$$ \left\{\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}{\bm{E}}\widehat{P}^{\perp}\|_{2}\leq n\lambda_{3}/4\right\}\bigcap\left\{{1\over\sqrt{n}}\left\|({\bm{X}}F^{*}+{\bm{W}}B^{*})\widehat{P}^{\perp}-{\bm{X}}\Theta^{*}\right\|_{F}\leq Rem_{5}\right\}, $$

by using $|\langle M,N\rangle|\leq\|M\|_{F}\|N\|_{F}$ for any commensurate matrices, we obtain

$$ {1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2}\leq{2\over\sqrt{n}}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}\cdot Rem_{5}+{\lambda_{3}\over 2}\left(3\|\Delta_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Delta_{S_{*}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right). $$

By rearranging terms, we have

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2}\left(1-{2Rem_{5}\over\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}/\sqrt{n}}\right)\leq{\lambda_{3}\over 2}\left(3\|\Delta_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Delta_{S_{*}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right). $$

When $\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}/\sqrt{n}\leq 4Rem_{5}$ , (B.12) holds. When $\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}/\sqrt{n}\geq 4Rem_{5}$ , we have

$$ {1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2}\leq{\lambda_{3}}\left(3\|\Delta_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Delta_{S_{*}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right). $$

Hence $\Delta\in\mathcal{C}(S_{*},3)\subseteq\mathcal{C}(S_{*},4)$ . Invoking (3.5) with $s=s_{*}$ and $\alpha=3$ yields

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2}\leq 3\lambda_{3}\|\Delta_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}} \displaystyle\leq 3\lambda_{3}\sqrt{s_{*}}\|\Delta_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{F}\leq{3\lambda_{3}\sqrt{s_{*}}\over\kappa(s_{*},3)}{1\over\sqrt{n}}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}, $$

which implies the first result on the event $\mathcal{E}^{\prime}\cap\mathcal{E}_{B^{*}}$ .

To show (B.13), note that $\kappa(s_{*},4)>0$ and consider two cases: (1) When $\Delta\in\mathcal{C}(S_{*},4)$ , from the definition of $\kappa(s_{*},4)$ , one has

$$ \displaystyle\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}} \displaystyle=\|\Delta_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+\|\Delta_{S_{*}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}} \displaystyle\leq 5\|\Delta_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}} \displaystyle\leq 5\sqrt{s_{*}}\|\Delta_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{F} \displaystyle\leq{5\sqrt{s_{*}}\over\kappa(s_{*},4)}{1\over\sqrt{n}}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}. $$

(2) When $\Delta\notin\mathcal{C}(S_{*},4)$ , we have $4\|\Delta_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}<\|\Delta_{S_{*}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}$ by definition. Plugging this into display (B.14), we have

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2}\leq{2\over\sqrt{n}}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}\cdot Rem_{5}-{\lambda_{3}\over 8}\|\Delta_{S_{*}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}. $$

It implies $\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}/\sqrt{n}\leq 2Rem_{5}$ and

$$ \lambda_{3}\|\Delta_{S_{*}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\leq{16\over\sqrt{n}}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}\cdot Rem_{5} $$

We thus obtain

$$ \displaystyle\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}} \displaystyle\leq{5\over 4}\|\Delta_{S_{*}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\leq 20{Rem_{5}\over\lambda_{3}}{1\over\sqrt{n}}\|{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}\leq 40{Rem_{5}^{2}\over\lambda_{3}}. $$

Combining these two cases and invoking (B.12) give the desired result on the event $\mathcal{E}^{\prime}\cap\mathcal{E}_{B^{*}}$ . Finally, invoking Lemmas 8 and 16 yield $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}^{\prime})\geq 1-\epsilon-2m^{-c^{\prime\prime}K}$ . This completes the proof. ∎

The following lemma gives that the probability of $\mathcal{E}^{\prime}$ on the event $\mathcal{E}_{B^{*}}$ . Recall that $Rem_{5}$ is defined in (B.11).

#### Lemma 8.

Under conditions of Theorem 6, on the event $\mathcal{E}_{B^{*}}=\{\|\widehat{P}-P_{B^{*}}\|_{F}\leq c\xi_{n}\}$ for some constant $c>0$ , the following holds with probability $1-2e^{-c^{\prime}K}$ for some constant $c^{\prime}>0$ ,

$$ {1\over\sqrt{n}}\left\|({\bm{X}}F^{*}+{\bm{W}}B^{*})\widehat{P}^{\perp}-{\bm{X}}\Theta^{*}\right\|_{F}\leq Rem_{5}. $$

By noting that $({\bm{X}}F^{*}+{\bm{W}}B^{*})P^{\perp}_{B^{*}}={\bm{X}}\Theta^{*}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle{1\over\sqrt{n}}\left\|({\bm{X}}F^{*}+{\bm{W}}B^{*})\widehat{P}^{\perp}-{\bm{X}}\Theta^{*}\right\|_{F} \displaystyle={1\over\sqrt{n}}\left\|({\bm{X}}F^{*}+{\bm{W}}B^{*})(\widehat{P}^{\perp}-P_{B^{*}}^{\perp})\right\|_{F} \displaystyle\leq{1\over\sqrt{n}}\|({\bm{X}}F^{*}+{\bm{W}}B^{*})\|_{op}\left\|\widehat{P}^{\perp}-P_{B^{*}}^{\perp}\right\|_{F} \displaystyle\leq{1\over\sqrt{n}}\Bigl(\|{\bm{X}}F^{*}\|_{op}+\|{\bm{W}}B^{*}\|_{op}\Big)c\xi_{n}, $$

where we have used $\|MN\|_{F}\leq\|M\|_{op}\|N\|_{F}$ for any commensurate matrices in the third line and the triangle inequality in the last line. For ${\bm{W}}B^{*}$ , invoking Lemma 17 gives

$$ {1\over n}\|{\bm{W}}B^{*}\|_{op}^{2}\leq\|(B^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}\|_{op}\left[1+C_{\gamma_{w}}\left(\sqrt{K\over n}\vee{K\over n}\right)\right] $$

with probability $1-2e^{-c^{\prime}K}$ for some constants $c^{\prime}>0$ and $C_{\gamma_{w}}$ depending on $\gamma_{w}$ only. This completes the proof. ∎

### B.5 Proof of Theorem 7: convergence rate of $\|\widehat{P}_{B^{*}}-P_{B^{*}}\|_{F}$ for homoscedastic case

Recall that $\widehat{P}_{B^{*}}=\widehat{U}\widehat{U}^{T}$ and $P_{B^{*}}=UU^{T}$ . Write

$$ M=(B^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}. $$

Applying Theorem 2 in [57] to $\Sigma_{\varepsilon}$ and $\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}$ with $d=s=K$ and $r=1$ yields

$$ \|\widehat{U}Q-U\|_{F}\leq{2^{3/2}\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\|_{F}\over\lambda_{K}(\Sigma_{\varepsilon})-\lambda_{K+1}(\Sigma_{\varepsilon})}={2^{3/2}\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\|_{F}\over\lambda_{K}(M)} $$

for some orthogonal matrix $Q$ . We also use the fact that $\Sigma_{E}=\tau^{2}{\bm{I}}_{m}$ and $\lambda_{K+1}(M)=0$ . Note that, for this $Q$ ,

$$ \|\widehat{U}\widehat{U}^{T}-UU^{T}\|_{F}\leq\|(\widehat{U}Q-U)Q^{T}\widehat{U}^{T}\|_{F}+\|U(\widehat{U}Q-U)^{T}\|_{F}=2\|\widehat{U}Q-U\|_{F}. $$

It then suffices to upper bound $\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\|_{F}$ . Notice that

$$ \displaystyle\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-{1\over n}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}} \displaystyle={1\over n}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\widehat{F})^{T}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\widehat{F})-{1\over n}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}} \displaystyle={1\over n}(\widehat{F}-F^{*})^{T}{\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{F}-F^{*})+{1\over n}(F^{*}-\widehat{F})^{T}{\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}}+{1\over n}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{X}}(F^{*}-\widehat{F}). $$

Recalling that (B.4), we have

$$ \displaystyle{\bm{X}}\widehat{F}-{\bm{X}}F^{*} \displaystyle=P_{\lambda_{2}}({\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}\Psi_{0})-{\bm{X}}L_{0}+Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0}) \displaystyle=P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}-Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L_{0}+Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0}) $$

for any $\Psi_{0}+L_{0}=F^{*}$ . By using formula $\|H^{T}H\|_{F}\leq\|H\|_{F}^{2}$ for any matrix $H$ and triangle inequality, we thus have

$$ \displaystyle\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\|_{F} \displaystyle\leq{1\over n}\left\|{\bm{X}}\widehat{F}-{\bm{X}}F^{*}\right\|_{F}^{2}+{2\over n}\left\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{F}-F^{*})\right\|_{F}+\left\|{1\over n}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\right\|_{F} \displaystyle\leq{1\over n}\left\|{\bm{X}}\widehat{F}-{\bm{X}}F^{*}\right\|_{F}^{2}+{2\over n}\left\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\right\|_{F}+{2\over n}\left\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L_{0}\right\|_{F} \displaystyle\qquad+{2\over n}\left\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0})\right\|_{F}+\left\|{1\over n}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\right\|_{F}. $$

We then study each terms on the right hand side. From Lemma 14, we have

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{F}\leq{1\over n}\left\|P_{\lambda_{2}}^{1/2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\right\|_{F}^{2}\leq{V_{\varepsilon}\over n}\left(\sqrt{\textrm{tr}(P_{\lambda_{2}})}+\sqrt{2\|P_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\log(m/\epsilon)}\right)^{2} \displaystyle{1\over n}\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}\leq\sqrt{V_{\varepsilon}\log(m/\epsilon)\over n}\sqrt{\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\cdot Rem_{2}(L_{0})} $$

with probability $1-2\epsilon$ . To bound the fourth term, first notice that

$$ {1\over n}\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0})\|_{F}\leq\max_{1\leq j\leq p}{1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}\cdot\|\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}. $$

Indeed, by writing $\Delta=\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0}$ , one has

$$ \displaystyle\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle=\sum_{\ell=1}^{m}\Delta_{\ell}^{T}{\bm{X}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}\Delta_{\ell} \displaystyle\leq\sum_{\ell=1}^{m}\sum_{i=1}^{p}|\Delta_{i\ell}|\sum_{j=1}^{p}|\Delta_{j\ell}|\max_{i,j}|{\bm{X}}_{i}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}_{j}| \displaystyle\leq\sum_{i=1}^{p}\sum_{j=1}^{p}\|\Delta_{i\cdot}\|_{2}\|\Delta_{j\cdot}\|_{2}\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle=\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}^{2}\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}^{2}. $$

Note that, on the event $\mathcal{E}$ defined in (B.7),

$$ \|\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\lesssim{\lambda_{1}s_{0}\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{0},4)}+{Rem_{2}(L_{0})\over\lambda_{1}} $$

from (B.23). Invoking (B.7) yields

$$ {1\over n}\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0})\|_{F}\lesssim Rem_{2}(L_{0})+{\lambda_{1}^{2}s_{0}\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{0},4)} $$

with probability $1-\epsilon^{\prime}$ . Finally, the last term can be upper bounded by invoking Lemma 18 as

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{\left\|{1\over n}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\right\|_{F}\leq cV_{\varepsilon}\left(\sqrt{\log m\over n}\vee{\log m\over n}\right)\right\}\geq 1-2m^{-c^{\prime}} $$

for some constant $c,c^{\prime}>0$ . Collecting terms and invoking Theorem 9 for $\|{\bm{X}}\widehat{F}-{\bm{X}}F^{*}\|_{F}^{2}/n$ yield, after using $\|P_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\leq 1$ , $\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\leq 1$ and Lemma 10 to simplify the results,

$$ \displaystyle\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\|_{F} \displaystyle\lesssim Rem_{2}(L_{0})+{\lambda_{1}^{2}s_{0}\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{0},4)}+{V_{\varepsilon}\over n}\left(\sqrt{\textrm{tr}(P_{\lambda_{2}})}+\sqrt{2\|P_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\log(m/\epsilon)}\right)^{2} \displaystyle\quad+\sqrt{V_{\varepsilon}\log(m/\epsilon)\over n}\sqrt{Rem_{2}(L_{0})}+V_{\varepsilon}\left(\sqrt{\log m\over n}\vee{\log m\over n}\right) \displaystyle\lesssim Rem_{2}(L_{0})+{\lambda_{1}^{2}s_{0}\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{0},4)}+{\textrm{tr}(P_{\lambda_{2}})V_{\varepsilon}\over n}+V_{\varepsilon}\left(\sqrt{\log(m/\epsilon)\over n}\vee{\log(m/\epsilon)\over n}\right) $$

with probability $1-3\epsilon-\epsilon^{\prime}-2m^{-c^{\prime}}$ . Recall the eigen-decomposition of $\widehat{\Sigma}=U\textrm{diag}(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{p})U^{T}$ with $U=(u_{1},\ldots,u_{K})$ . We have

$$ \displaystyle\textrm{tr}(P_{\lambda_{2}})=\textrm{tr}\left[{1\over n}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{\Sigma}+\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}\right]=\sum_{k=1}^{q}{\sigma_{k}\over\sigma_{k}+\lambda_{2}}, \displaystyle Rem_{2}(L_{0})=\sum_{k}{\lambda_{2}\sigma_{k}\over\sigma_{k}+\lambda_{2}}u_{k}^{T}L_{0}L_{0}^{T}u_{k}\leq{\lambda_{2}\sigma_{1}\over\sigma_{1}+\lambda_{2}}\|L_{0}\|_{F}^{2}. $$

By invoking Lemma 10 together with the choice of $\lambda_{1}$ as (3.4), we further have

$$ {\lambda_{1}^{2}s_{0}\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{0},4)}\lesssim{\sigma_{1}+\lambda_{2}\over\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}^{2}s_{0}\over\kappa^{2}(s_{0},4)}\lesssim{\lambda_{2}(\sigma_{1}+\lambda_{2})\over(\sigma_{q}+\lambda_{2})^{2}}{s_{0}V_{\varepsilon}\log N\over\kappa^{2}(s_{0},4)n} $$

Take $\varepsilon=m^{-c^{\prime}}$ and use $\log m\leq n$ in (B.18) to complete the proof. ∎

### B.6 Lemma 9 used in the proof of Theorem 7

The following lemma provides the rate of $\|\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}$ where $\widehat{\Psi}$ is obtained in (2.3). Furthermore, the proof also reveals that Lemma 9 holds if $\lambda_{1}$ is replaced by any $\widetilde{\lambda}_{1}\geq\lambda_{1}$ .

#### Lemma 9.

Under conditions of Corollary 5, choose $\lambda_{1}$ as (3.4) and any $\lambda_{2}\geq 0$ such that $P_{\lambda_{2}}$ exists. With probability $1-\epsilon-\epsilon^{\prime}$ ,

$$ \|\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\lesssim{\lambda_{1}s_{0}\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{0},4)}+{Rem_{2}(L_{0})\over\lambda_{1}} $$

where $L_{0}=F^{*}-\Psi_{0}$ and $Rem_{2}(L_{0})$ is defined in Theorem 4.

We prove (B.21) by working on the event $\mathcal{E}$ defined in (B.7). From (B.10),

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}(\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0})\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle\leq\max\left\{16\lambda_{2}\textrm{tr}\left[L_{0}^{T}\widehat{\Sigma}(\widehat{\Sigma}+\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}L_{0}\right],{4\lambda_{1}^{2}\over\kappa_{1}^{2}(1/2,\Psi_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})}\right\} \displaystyle\lesssim Rem_{2}(L_{0})+{\lambda_{1}^{2}s_{0}\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{0},3)}. $$

by invoking the first result of Lemma 10 with $c=1/2$ . Write $\Delta:=\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi_{0}$ and consider two cases. (1) When $\Delta\in\mathcal{C}(S_{0},4)$ with $S_{0}=\{1\leq j\leq p:\|[\Psi_{0}]_{j\cdot}\|_{2}\neq 0\}$ , it follows from the definitions of $\mathcal{C}(S_{0},4)$ and $\widetilde{\kappa}(s_{0},4)$ that

$$ \displaystyle\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}} \displaystyle\leq 5\|\Delta_{S_{0}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\leq 5\sqrt{s_{0}}\|\Delta_{S_{0}\cdot}\|_{F}\leq 5{\sqrt{s_{0}}\over\widetilde{\kappa}(s_{0},4)}{1\over\sqrt{n}}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}. $$

(2) When $\Delta\notin\mathcal{C}(S_{0},4)$ , it implies $\|\Delta_{S_{0}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}>4\|\Delta_{S_{0}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}.$ From (B.6), by invoking $\mathcal{E}$ , we obtain

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle\leq{2\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}+{\lambda_{1}\over 2}\left(3\|\Delta_{S_{0}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Delta_{S_{0}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\right) \displaystyle\leq{2\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}-{\lambda_{1}\over 8}\|\Delta_{S_{0}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}. $$

This implies $\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}\leq 2\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}$ and

$$ \|\Delta_{S_{0}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\leq{16\over\lambda_{1}}\cdot{1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}\|\widetilde{X}\Delta\|_{F}\leq{32\over\lambda_{1}}{1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}^{2}. $$

Using $\|\Delta_{S_{0}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}>4\|\Delta_{S_{0}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}$ again yields

$$ \displaystyle\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\leq{5\over 4}\|\Delta_{S_{0}^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\leq{40\over\lambda_{1}}{1\over n}\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}L_{0}\|_{F}^{2}. $$

Combining these two cases and invoking (B.9) with $L_{0}$ and (B.22) give

$$ \displaystyle\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}} \displaystyle\lesssim{\sqrt{s_{0}}\over\widetilde{\kappa}(s_{0},4)}\left(\sqrt{Rem_{2}(L_{0})}+{\lambda_{1}\sqrt{s_{0}}\over\widetilde{\kappa}(s_{0},3)}\right)+{Rem_{2}(L_{0})\over\lambda_{1}} \displaystyle\lesssim{\lambda_{1}s_{0}\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{0},4)}+{Rem_{2}(L_{0})\over\lambda_{1}} $$

where we also use $\widetilde{\kappa}(s_{0},3)\geq\widetilde{\kappa}(s_{0},4)$ to derive the last inequality. We then conclude the proof by recalling that $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E})=1-\epsilon^{\prime}$ . ∎

### B.7 Proof of Theorem 10: convergence rate of $\|\widetilde{P}_{B^{*}}-P_{B^{*}}\|_{F}$ for heteroscedastic case

Let $M=(B^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}$ . From (B.16) and by using $\Sigma_{\varepsilon}=M+\Sigma_{E}$ , one has

$$ \displaystyle\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}=M+\Delta_{1}+\Delta_{2} $$

where $\Delta_{1}=\Sigma_{E}=\textrm{diag}(\tau_{1}^{2},\ldots,\tau_{m}^{2})$ and

$$ \displaystyle\Delta_{2} \displaystyle={1\over n}(\widehat{F}-F^{*})^{T}{\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{F}-F^{*})+{1\over n}(F^{*}-\widehat{F})^{T}{\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}} \displaystyle\quad+{1\over n}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{X}}(F^{*}-\widehat{F})+{1\over n}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}. $$

We aim to apply Theorem 13 with $N=\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}$ , $M=M$ , $Z=\Delta_{1}+\Delta_{2}$ , $\widehat{V}=\widetilde{U}$ and $V=U$ . Observe that $\|\Gamma(\Delta_{1})\|_{F}=0$ , that is, the off-diagonal elements of $\Delta_{1}$ are zero, and $\|\Delta_{2}\|_{F}=\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\|_{F}$ from (B.16). Invoking (B.18) yields

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{\|\Delta_{2}\|_{F}\leq Rem(P_{B^{*}})\cdot\lambda_{K}(M)\right\}\geq 1-\epsilon^{\prime}-5m^{-c^{\prime}} $$

with $Rem(P_{B^{*}})$ defined in (3.14). We then work on the event that the above display holds. Recall that $\Gamma(\Delta_{2})$ denotes the matrix with off-diagonal elements equal to $\Delta_{2}$ and diagonal elements equal to zero. Since $Rem(P_{B^{*}})\leq c\sqrt{K}$ implies $\|\Gamma(\Delta_{2})\|_{F}\leq\|\Delta_{2}\|_{F}\leq c\sqrt{K}\lambda_{K}(M)$ , in conjunction with condition (4.2), an application of Theorem 13 with $N=\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}$ , $M=M$ , $Z=\Delta_{1}+\Delta_{2}$ , $\widehat{V}=\widetilde{U}$ and $V=U$ gives

$$ \|\sin\Theta(\widetilde{U},U)\|_{F}\lesssim{\|\Gamma(\Delta_{2})\|_{F}\over\lambda_{K}(M)}\wedge\sqrt{K}\leq{\|\Delta_{2}\|_{F}\over\lambda_{K}(M)}. $$

Finally, using the inequality

$$ \|\widetilde{P}_{B^{*}}-P_{B^{*}}\|_{F}=\|\widetilde{U}\widetilde{U}^{T}-UU^{T}\|_{F}\leq 2\|\sin\Theta(\widetilde{U},U)\|_{F}. $$

and (B.24) again concludes the proof.∎

### B.8 Proof of Theorem 11: consistency of using PCA to estimate $P_{B^{*}}$ in the presence of heteroscedasticity

The proof follows the same arguments as that of Theorem 7. The first difference is to apply Theorem 2 in [57] to $\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}$ and $\Pi:=B^{*T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}+\bar{\tau}^{2}{\bm{I}}_{m}$ with $d=s=K$ and $r=1$ to obtain

$$ \|\widehat{U}Q-U\|_{F}\leq{2^{3/2}\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Pi\|_{F}\over\lambda_{K}(\Pi)-\lambda_{K+1}(\Pi)}={2^{3/2}\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Pi\|_{F}\over\lambda_{K}(\Pi)}. $$

The second difference from the proof of Theorem 7 is to upper bound the numerator as

by adding and subtracting $\Sigma_{\varepsilon}$ and using $\Sigma_{\varepsilon}=\Pi+\Sigma_{E}-\bar{\tau}^{2}{\bm{I}}_{m}$ . Since the results in Theorem 4 still hold in the heteroscedasticity case, $\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\|_{F}$ can be bounded by (B.18). Then the proof is completed by using

$$ \|\Sigma_{E}-\bar{\tau}^{2}{\bm{I}}_{m}\|_{F}^{2}=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\left(\tau_{j}^{2}-\bar{\tau}^{2}\right)^{2}. $$

### B.9 Proof of Theorem 12: selection of $K$

Write $M=(B^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}$ and its eigenvalues as $\Lambda_{1}\geq\Lambda_{2}\geq\cdots\geq\Lambda_{K}$ and $\Lambda_{j}=0$ for $j>K$ . Recall that $\widehat{\lambda}_{1}\geq\widehat{\lambda}_{2}\geq\cdots\geq\widehat{\lambda}_{m}$ are the eigenvalues of $\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}$ . By Weyl’s inequality, we have

$$ |\widehat{\lambda}_{j}-\Lambda_{j}|\leq\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-M\|_{op} $$

for all $1\leq j\leq m$ . We work on the event $\{\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\|_{F}\lesssim Rem(P_{B^{*}})\Lambda_{K}\}$ which, from the proof of Theorem 7, holds with probability $1-\epsilon^{\prime}-5m^{-c}$ for some constant $c>0$ . Note that

$$ \displaystyle\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-M\|_{op} \displaystyle\leq\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\varepsilon}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\|_{F}+\|\Sigma_{E}\|_{op}\lesssim Rem(P_{B^{*}})\Lambda_{K}+\max_{1\leq j\leq m}\tau_{j}^{2}. $$

We thus conclude

$$ |\widehat{\lambda}_{j}-\Lambda_{j}|\lesssim\max_{1\leq j\leq m}\tau_{j}^{2}+Rem(P_{B^{*}})\Lambda_{K} $$

for $1\leq j\leq m$ . Since $(b)$ of Assumption 2 implies $\Lambda_{j}\asymp m$ for $1\leq j\leq K$ , by also using $Rem(P_{B^{*}})=o(1)$ and $\max_{j}\tau_{j}^{2}=O(1)$ , we have $\widehat{\lambda}_{j}\asymp m$ . This concludes $\widehat{\lambda}_{j+1}/\widehat{\lambda}_{j}\asymp 1$ for $1\leq k\leq{K-1}$ . On the other hand, since $\widehat{\lambda}_{K+1}=O(\max_{j}\tau_{j}^{2}+Rem(P_{B^{*}})\Lambda_{K})$ , we further obtain $\widehat{\lambda}_{K+1}/\widehat{\lambda}_{K}=O(\max_{j}\tau_{j}^{2}/m+Rem(P_{B^{*}}))$ . This completes the proof. ∎

We establish the connection between the impact factor defined in (3.1) and the RE conditions of $\widetilde{\bm{X}}$ and ${\bm{X}}$ . #### Lemma 10.

For any given $\Psi_{0}$ with row-sparsity $s_{0}$ and any constant $c\in(0,1)$ , one has

$$ \kappa_{1}(c,\Psi_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})\geq{\widetilde{\kappa}(s_{0},\alpha_{c})\over(1+c)\sqrt{s_{0}}}\geq\sqrt{\lambda_{2}\over\sigma_{1}+\lambda_{2}}\cdot{\kappa(s_{0},\alpha_{c})\over(1+c)\sqrt{s_{0}}} $$

with $\alpha_{c}=(1+c)/(1-c)$ , and

$$ \max_{1\leq j\leq p}M_{jj}\leq\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\widehat{\Sigma}_{jj}\left(\lambda_{2}\over\sigma_{q}+\lambda_{2}\right)^{2}. $$

As a result, we have

$$ {\max_{1\leq j\leq p}M_{jj}\over\kappa_{1}^{2}(1/2,\Psi_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})}\leq{9s_{0}\over 4\kappa^{2}(s_{0},3)}\max_{j}\widehat{\Sigma}_{jj}\cdot{\lambda_{2}(\sigma_{1}+\lambda_{2})\over(\sigma_{q}+\lambda_{2})^{2}}. $$

We first prove

$$ \kappa_{1}(c,\Psi_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})\geq{\widetilde{\kappa}(s_{0},\alpha_{c})\over(1+c)\sqrt{s_{0}}}. $$

$$ \displaystyle 0 \displaystyle\leq\|\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Psi_{0}+\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+c\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}} \displaystyle\leq\|\Delta_{S\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Delta_{S^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+c\|\Delta_{S\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+c\|\Delta_{S^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}} \displaystyle=(1+c)\|\Delta_{S\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-(1-c)\|\Delta_{S^{c}\cdot}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}, $$

which implies $\Delta\in\mathcal{C}(S,\alpha_{c})$ . Note the above display also implies

$$ \|\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Psi_{0}+\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+c\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\leq\sqrt{s_{0}}(1+c)\|\Delta_{S\cdot}\|_{F}. $$

We thus have

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{\kappa}(s_{0},\alpha_{c}) \displaystyle=\min_{\begin{subarray}{c}S\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots,p\}\\
|S|\leq s_{0}\end{subarray}}\min_{\Delta\in\mathcal{C}(S,\alpha)}{\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}/\sqrt{n}\over\|\Delta_{S\cdot}\|_{F}} \displaystyle\leq\min_{\begin{subarray}{c}S\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots,p\}\\
|S|\leq s_{0}\end{subarray}}\min_{\Delta\in\mathcal{C}(S,\alpha)}{(1+c)\sqrt{s_{0}}\cdot\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}/\sqrt{n}\over\|\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Psi_{0}+\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+c\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}} \displaystyle\leq\min_{\Delta\in\mathcal{R}(c,\Psi_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2})}{(1+c)\sqrt{s_{0}}\cdot\|\widetilde{\bm{X}}\Delta\|_{F}/\sqrt{n}\over\|\Psi_{0}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}-\|\Psi_{0}+\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}+c\|\Delta\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}} \displaystyle=(1+c)\sqrt{s_{0}}\kappa_{1}(c,\Psi_{0},\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}). $$

We then prove the second inequality of the first statement. Since

by using Fact 1 in the second line, it follows that

We then show the second statement. From Fact 1 and $\widehat{\Sigma}=U\textrm{diag}(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{q})U^{T}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle{\rm Err}(P_{B^{*}}) \displaystyle=\min\Bigg\{{\sigma_{1}R_{*}\over m}+{Ks_{*}\over n},~{qK\over n},~\sqrt{{(p+\sigma_{1}s_{*})KR_{*}\over nm}}+{Ks_{*}\over n}\Bigg\}+{K\over\sqrt{n}} \displaystyle\lesssim\min\Bigg\{{R_{*}\over m}+{pK\over n},~{pK\over n},~\sqrt{{R_{*}\over m}\cdot{pK\over n}}+{pK\over n}\Bigg\}+{K\over\sqrt{n}} \displaystyle\leq{pK\over n}+{K\over\sqrt{n}}. $$

Using $p\asymp s_{*}$ gives

$$ \sqrt{s_{*}(m+s_{*})\over m}\cdot{\rm Err}(P_{B^{*}})\lessapprox\sqrt{p(m+p)\over m}\left({pK\over n}+{K\over\sqrt{n}}\right). $$

The result of $p<n$ then follows by (C.7) and $K=O(\sqrt{p}\wedge\sqrt{n/p})$ .

To prove the result of $p\geq n$ , note that

$$ \displaystyle{\rm Err}(P_{B^{*}}) \displaystyle\leq\min\Bigg\{\sigma_{1}{R_{*}\over m},~\sqrt{{(p+\sigma_{1}s_{*})KR_{*}\over nm}}\Bigg\}+{Ks_{*}\over n}+{K\over\sqrt{n}}. $$

Condition $K=O(\sqrt{s_{*}}\wedge\sqrt{n/s_{*}}\wedge m)$ implies

$$ \sqrt{s_{*}(m+s_{*})\over m}\left({K\over\sqrt{n}}+{Ks_{*}\over n}\right)=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}O\left(s_{*}/\sqrt{n}\right)&\text{if }s_{*}=O(m);\\
O\left(s_{*}/\sqrt{n}+(s_{*}/\sqrt{n})^{2}\right)&\text{if }m=O(1).\end{array}\right. $$

The desired result then follows. ∎

Note that $\Theta^{*}=\Psi^{*}$ when $\Psi^{*}P_{B^{*}}=0$ . As a result, both $\Psi^{*}$ and $L^{*}$ are identifiable. From Lemma 9, we have

$$ \displaystyle\|\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi^{*}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}=O_{p}\left({\widetilde{\lambda}_{1}s_{*}\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{*},4)}+{Rem_{2}(L^{*})\over\widetilde{\lambda}_{1}}\right) $$

for any $\widetilde{\lambda}_{1}\geq\lambda_{1}$ with $\lambda_{1}$ defined in (3.4). For a suitable choice of $\widetilde{\lambda}_{1}$ , we can deduce that

$$ \|\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi^{*}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}=O_{p}\left({\lambda_{1}s_{*}\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{*},4)}+\sqrt{{s_{*}Rem_{2}(L^{*})\over\widetilde{\kappa}^{2}(s_{*},4)}}\right) $$

By Lemma 10 and (B.19) together with $V_{\varepsilon}=O(Km)$ and $[\kappa(s_{*},4)]^{-1}=O(1)$ under Assumption 2, we have

$$ {1\over\sqrt{m}}\|\widehat{\Psi}-\Psi^{*}\|_{\ell_{1}/\ell_{2}}\lessapprox{\sigma_{1}+\lambda_{2}\over\sigma_{q}+\lambda_{2}}\cdot{s_{*}\sqrt{K}\over\sqrt{n}}+\sqrt{{s_{*}\sigma_{1}R_{*}\over m}}. $$

The result then follows by taking $\lambda_{2}\gtrsim\sigma_{1}$ . ∎

### C.4 Lemma used in Section 3.4

The following lemma provides the upper bound of $n^{-1}\|{\bm{X}}F^{*}\|_{op}^{2}$ . Recall that $L^{*}=A^{*}B^{*}$ with $A^{*}$ defined in (1.3). Without loss of generality, we can assume $Y$ , $X$ and $Z$ are centered such that

$$ A^{*}=\Sigma^{-1}\Sigma_{XZ} $$

by writing $\Sigma_{XZ}=\text{Cov}(X,Z)$ . Recall that $\Sigma=\text{Cov}(X)$ , $\Sigma_{Z}=\text{Cov}(Z)$ and $S_{*}=\{1\leq j\leq p:\|\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\|_{2}\neq 0\}$ .

#### Lemma 12.

Suppose $\Sigma^{-1/2}{\bm{X}}_{i\cdot}$ are i.i.d. $\gamma_{X}$ sub-Gaussian random vectors for $1\leq i\leq n$ where $\gamma_{X}$ is some positive constant. Further assume $\|\Sigma_{S_{*}S_{*}}\|_{op}=O(1)$ , $\|\Sigma_{Z}\|_{op}=O(1)$ , $K=O(n)$ , $s_{*}=O(n)$ and $\|B^{*}\|_{op}^{2}=O(m)$ . Then

$$ {1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}F^{*}\|_{op}^{2}=O_{p}(s_{*}+m). $$

First, we have

$$ \|{\bm{X}}F^{*}\|_{op}\leq\|{\bm{X}}\Psi^{*}\|_{op}+\|{\bm{X}}L^{*}\|_{op}. $$

To bound the first term, one has

$$ \|{\bm{X}}\Psi^{*}\|_{op}=\|{\bm{X}}_{S_{*}}\|_{op}\|\Psi^{*}_{S_{*}\cdot}\|_{op}. $$

Since $\Sigma^{-1/2}{\bm{X}}_{i\cdot}$ are i.i.d. $\gamma_{X}$ sub-Gaussian, Theorem 5.39 in [55] yields

$$ {1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}_{S_{*}}\|_{op}^{2}={1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}_{S_{*}}^{T}{\bm{X}}_{S_{*}}\|_{op}=O_{p}\left(\|\Sigma_{S_{*}S_{*}}\|_{op}\left(1+{s_{*}\over n}\right)\right). $$

Invoking $\|\Sigma_{S_{*}S_{*}}\|_{op}=O(1)$ and $s_{*}=O(n)$ together with $\|\Psi^{*}\|_{op}^{2}=O(s_{*}+m)$ yields

$$ {1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}_{S_{*}}\|_{op}^{2}=O_{p}(m+s_{*}). $$

To bound $\|{\bm{X}}L^{*}\|_{op}\leq\|{\bm{X}}A^{*}\|_{op}\|B^{*}\|_{op}$ , recall that $A^{*}=\Sigma^{-1}\Sigma_{XZ}.$ The fact that $\Sigma^{-1/2}{\bm{X}}_{i\cdot}$ is $\gamma_{X}$ sub-Gaussian implies $A^{*T}{\bm{X}}_{i\cdot}$ is $\gamma_{X}\sqrt{\|\Sigma_{ZX}\Sigma^{-1}\Sigma_{XZ}\|_{op}}$ sub-Gaussian (see, for instance, [55]), hence $\gamma_{X}\sqrt{\|\Sigma_{Z}\|_{op}}$ sub-Gaussian. By using Theorem 5.39 in [55] again, one has

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{{1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}A^{*}\|_{op}^{2}\lesssim\gamma_{X}^{2}\left(1+{K\over n}\right)\right\}\geq 1-2e^{-cK}. $$

In conjunction with $\|B^{*}\|_{op}^{2}=O(m)$ , we then conclude

$$ {1\over n}\|{\bm{X}}L^{*}\|_{op}^{2}=O(m). $$

This completes the proof. ∎

### C.5 Proofs of Lemmas 3 and 4 in [10]

Let $G\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times m}$ be a random matrix whose entries are i.i.d. $N(0,1)$ . Write its SVD as $G=V_{G}D_{G}U_{G}^{T}$ where $U_{G}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times K}$ contains the $K$ right singular vectors. Since $GQ$ has the same distribution as $G$ for any orthogonal matrix $Q\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}$ , columns of $U_{G}$ are uniformly distributed over the families of $K$ orthonormal vectors. Hence $U_{G}$ has the same distribution as $U$ and it remains to show

$$ \left\|U_{G}U_{G}^{T}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right\|_{2}^{2}=O_{p}\left(\left\|\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right\|_{2}^{2}{K\over m}\right). $$

To this end, we have

$$ \displaystyle\left\|U_{G}U_{G}^{T}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle=\left\|U_{G}^{T}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right\|_{2}^{2}=\left\|D_{G}^{-1}V_{G}^{T}G\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right\|_{2}^{2}\leq{\|G\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\|_{2}^{2}\over\lambda_{K}(GG^{T})}. $$

Concentration inequalities for random matrices with i.i.d. Gaussian entries yield (see, for instance, [55, Corollary 3.35])

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{\lambda_{K}(GG^{T})\geq(\sqrt{m}-\sqrt{K}-t)^{2}\right\}\geq 1-2e^{-t^{2}/2},\quad\forall t>0. $$

By noting that $G\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\sim N(0,\|\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\|_{2}^{2}\cdot{\bm{I}}_{K})$ , invoking Lemma 19 yields

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{{\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}}^{T}GG^{T}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}>\|\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\|_{2}^{2}\left(\sqrt{K}+\sqrt{2t}\right)^{2}\right\}\leq e^{-t},\quad\forall t>0. $$

Combining these two displays and using $K=o(m)$ complete the proof. The proof of

$$ \left|e_{\ell}^{T}U_{G}U_{G}^{T}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right|=O_{p}\left(\left\|\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right\|_{2}{K\over m}\right), $$

for any $1\leq\ell\leq m$ , follows immediately by noting that

$$ \left|e_{\ell}^{T}U_{G}U_{G}^{T}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right|\leq\left\|U_{G}U_{G}^{T}e_{\ell}\right\|_{2}\left\|U_{G}U_{G}^{T}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right\|_{2}. $$

The second statement follows immediately from the first result and $\|\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\|_{2}^{2}\leq m\|\Psi^{*}\|_{\infty}^{2}=O(m)$ ∎

Pick any $1\leq j\leq p$ . We have

$$ \displaystyle\left\|P_{B^{*}}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle=\left\|{B^{*}}^{T}(B^{*}{B^{*}}^{T})^{-1}B^{*}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle\leq\|{B^{*}}^{T}(B^{*}{B^{*}}^{T})^{-1}\|_{op}^{2}\|B^{*}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle=\lambda_{K}^{-1}(B^{*}{B^{*}}^{T})\sum_{k=1}^{K}|{B^{*}_{k\cdot}}^{T}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}|^{2}. $$

The result follows from $\lambda_{K}(B^{*}{B^{*}}^{T})\geq c^{\prime}m$ and $|{B^{*}_{k\cdot}}^{T}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}|\leq d\|\Psi^{*}\|_{\infty}\|B^{*}\|_{\infty}$ .

Pick $1\leq\ell\leq m$ . Similar arguments yield

$$ \displaystyle\left|e_{\ell}^{T}P_{B^{*}}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right| \displaystyle=\left|e_{\ell}^{T}{B^{*}}^{T}(B^{*}{B^{*}}^{T})^{-1}B^{*}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\right| \displaystyle\leq\|{B^{*}}e_{\ell}\|_{2}\|(B^{*}{B^{*}}^{T})^{-1}\|_{op}^{2}\|B^{*}\Psi^{*}_{j\cdot}\|_{2} \displaystyle\leq Kd~{\|\Psi^{*}\|_{\infty}\|B^{*}\|_{\infty}^{2}\over\lambda_{K}(B^{*}{B^{*}}^{T})}. $$

The proof is complete. ∎

### C.6 Technical lemmas for controlling the stochastic terms

Recall that ${\bm{\varepsilon}}={\bm{W}}B^{*}+{\bm{E}}$ and $P_{\lambda_{2}}$ , $Q_{\lambda_{2}}$ are defined in (2.4). Further recall that

$$ V_{\varepsilon}=\textrm{tr}(\Gamma_{\varepsilon})=\gamma_{w}^{2}\|\Sigma_{W}^{1/2}B^{*}\|_{F}^{2}+m\gamma_{e}^{2},\qquad\Gamma_{\varepsilon}=\gamma_{w}^{2}B^{*T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}+\gamma_{e}^{2}{\bm{I}}_{m}. $$

We first state a lemma which studies the tail behaviour of ${\bm{\varepsilon}}$ .

#### Lemma 13.

Under Assumption 1, ${\bm{\varepsilon}}_{ij}$ is $\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}}$ sub-Gaussian for any $i\in[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $j\in[m]$ with

$$ \gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}}^{2}=\gamma_{w}^{2}\left[(B_{j}^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B_{j}^{*}\right]+\gamma_{e}^{2}. $$

Furthermore, the random vector ${\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}$ is $\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}}$ sub-Gaussian for any $j\in[m]$ and the random vector $\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{i\cdot}$ is sub-Gaussian with sub-Gaussian constant equal to $1$ for any $i\in[n]$

Fix any $i\in[n]$ and $j\in[m]$ . For any $t\geq 0$ , by the independence of ${\bm{E}}$ and ${\bm{W}}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\exp(t{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{ij})] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\exp(t{\bm{W}}_{i\cdot}^{T}B_{j}^{*})]\cdot\mathbb{E}[\exp(t{\bm{E}}_{ij})] \displaystyle\leq\exp\left(t^{2}\gamma_{w}^{2}\|\Sigma_{W}^{1/2}B_{j}^{*}\|_{2}^{2}/2\right)\exp(t^{2}\gamma_{e}^{2}/2) $$

where we use Assumption 1 in the second line. This proves the first claim. The second claim follows immediately from the i.i.d. property over $1\leq i\leq n$ . To prove the third result, for any $i\in[n]$ and any fixed $u\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(u^{T}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{i\cdot}\right)\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(u^{T}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}B^{*T}{\bm{W}}_{i\cdot}\right)\right]\cdot\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(u^{T}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}{\bm{E}}_{i\cdot}\right)\right] \displaystyle\leq\exp\left\{{1\over 2}\left[\gamma_{w}^{2}u^{T}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}B^{*T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}u+\gamma_{e}^{2}u^{T}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}{\bm{I}}_{m}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}u\right]\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left(\gamma_{w}^{2}\|u\|_{2}^{2}/2\right). $$

We used the independence between ${\bm{W}}$ and ${\bm{E}}$ in the first equality and used Assumption 1 to derive the second line. This completes the proof. ∎

We present several lemmas which control different terms related with ${\bm{\varepsilon}}$ , ${\bm{W}}$ and ${\bm{E}}$ . The following lemma states the deviation inequality of $\|P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{F}^{2}$ , $\|P_{\lambda_{2}}^{1/2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{F}^{2}$ and $\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L^{*}\|_{F}$ .

#### Lemma 14.

Under Assumption 1, one has

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{P}\left\{\left\|P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\right\|_{F}^{2}\leq V_{\varepsilon}\left(\sqrt{\textrm{tr}(P_{\lambda_{2}}^{2})}+\sqrt{2\|P_{\lambda_{2}}^{2}\|_{op}\log(m/\epsilon)}\right)^{2}\right\}\geq 1-\epsilon \displaystyle\mathbb{P}\left\{\left\|P_{\lambda_{2}}^{1/2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\right\|_{F}^{2}\leq V_{\varepsilon}\left(\sqrt{\textrm{tr}(P_{\lambda_{2}})}+\sqrt{2\|P_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\log(m/\epsilon)}\right)^{2}\right\}\geq 1-\epsilon \displaystyle\mathbb{P}\left\{\left\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L^{*}\right\|_{F}\leq\sqrt{nV_{\varepsilon}}\sqrt{\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}Rem_{2}(L^{*})\log(m/\epsilon)}\right\}\geq 1-\epsilon. $$

We now prove the first result. Note that $\|P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{F}^{2}=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\|P_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}\|_{2}^{2}$ . Pick any $j\in[m]$ . Since ${\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}$ is $\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}}$ sub-Gaussian from Lemma 13, applying Lemma 19 with $\gamma_{\xi}=\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}}$ and $K=P_{\lambda_{2}}^{2}$ yields

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}^{T}P_{\lambda_{2}}^{2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}>\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}}^{2}\left(\sqrt{\textrm{tr}(P_{\lambda_{2}}^{2})}+\sqrt{2\|P_{\lambda_{2}}^{2}\|_{op}t}\right)^{2}\right\}\leq e^{-t}, $$

for all $t\geq 0$ . Since $\sum_{j=1}^{m}\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}}^{2}=V_{\varepsilon}$ , choosing $t=\log(m/\epsilon)$ and taking the union bounds over $1\leq j\leq m$ complete the proof of the first result. By the same arguments, the second result follows immediately, and we also have

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{\left\|{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L^{*}\right\|_{F}^{2}\leq{V_{\varepsilon}}\left(\sqrt{\textrm{tr}(D)}+\sqrt{2\|D\|_{op}\log(m/\epsilon)}\right)^{2}\right\}\geq 1-\epsilon $$

where $D=Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L^{*}(L^{*})^{T}{\bm{X}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}$ . The third result then follows by observing that

$$ \textrm{tr}(D)\leq\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}L^{*}\|_{F}^{2}\leq n\|Q_{\lambda_{2}}\|_{op}\cdot Rem_{2}(L^{*}) $$

from (B.5) and $\|D\|_{op}\leq\textrm{tr}(D)$ . ∎

The following lemma provides the deviation inequality of $\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}$ . Recall that $M=n^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}^{2}{\bm{X}}$ and $\Gamma_{\varepsilon}=\gamma_{w}^{2}B^{*T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}+\gamma_{e}^{2}{\bm{I}}_{m}$ .

#### Lemma 15.

Under Assumption 1, with probability $1-\epsilon$ , one has

$$ \max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}^{2}\leq\left(\sqrt{{\rm tr}(\Gamma_{\varepsilon})}+\sqrt{2\|\Gamma_{\varepsilon}\|_{op}\log(p/\epsilon)}\right)^{2}n\max_{1\leq j\leq p}M_{jj}. $$

Fix any $1\leq j\leq p$ . Notice that

$$ \|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}^{2}={\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}_{j}. $$

We first show that $\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}_{j}$ is $\sqrt{nM_{jj}}$ sub-Gaussian. By independence across $i\in[n]$ , we have, for any $v\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(v^{T}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}_{j}\right)\right] \displaystyle=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(v^{T}\Gamma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{i\cdot}e_{i}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}_{j}\right)\right] \displaystyle\leq\prod_{i=1}^{n}\exp\left(\|v\|_{2}^{2}e_{i}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}_{j}{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}e_{i}/2\right) \displaystyle=\exp(\|v\|_{2}^{2}nM_{jj}/2). $$

We used Lemma 13 to derive the second line. Then invoke Lemma 19 with $\gamma_{\xi}=\sqrt{nM_{jj}}$ and $K=\Gamma_{\varepsilon}$ gives

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{\varepsilon}}\|_{2}^{2}>nM_{jj}\left(\sqrt{\textrm{tr}(\Gamma_{\varepsilon})}+\sqrt{2\|\Gamma_{\varepsilon}\|_{op}t}\right)^{2}\right\}\leq e^{-t},\quad\text{for all }t\geq 0. $$

Choose $t=\log(p/\epsilon)$ and take the union bounds over $j\in[p]$ to complete the proof. ∎

The next tail inequality is for $\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}{\bm{E}}\|_{2}$ , derived based on the quadtratic form of a sub-Gaussian random vector.

#### Lemma 16.

Under Assumption 1, with probability $1-\epsilon$ , one has

$$ \max_{1\leq j\leq p}\|{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}{\bm{E}}\|_{2}^{2}\leq\gamma_{e}^{2}\left(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{2\log(p/\epsilon)}\right)^{2}n\max_{1\leq j\leq p}\widehat{\Sigma}_{jj}. $$

Pick any $1\leq j\leq p$ . Note that ${\bm{E}}^{T}{\bm{X}}_{j}$ is $\gamma_{e}\sqrt{n\widehat{\Sigma}_{jj}}$ sub-Gaussian. Indeed, for any $u\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\exp(\langle u,{\bm{E}}^{T}{\bm{X}}_{j}\rangle)] \displaystyle=\prod_{t=1}^{n}\prod_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{E}[\exp(u_{i}{\bm{X}}_{tj}{\bm{E}}_{ti})] \displaystyle\leq\prod_{t=1}^{n}\prod_{i=1}^{m}\exp(u_{i}^{2}{\bm{X}}_{tj}^{2}\gamma_{e}^{2}/2)] \displaystyle=\exp(\|u\|_{2}^{2}{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}{\bm{X}}_{j}\gamma_{e}^{2}/2) $$

by using the independence of entries of ${\bm{E}}$ and ${\bm{E}}_{ti}$ is $\gamma_{e}$ sub-Gaussian. Applying Lemma 19 with $K={\bm{I}}_{m}$ and $\gamma_{\xi}=\gamma_{e}\sqrt{n\widehat{\Sigma}_{jj}}$ gives

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{{\bm{X}}_{j}^{T}{\bm{E}}{\bm{E}}^{T}{\bm{X}}_{j}>\gamma_{e}^{2}n\widehat{\Sigma}_{jj}\left(\sqrt{m}+\sqrt{2t}\right)^{2}\right\}\leq e^{-t}. $$

Choosing $t=\log(p/\epsilon)$ and taking the union bounds over $1\leq j\leq p$ conclude the proof. ∎

The following lemma states the tail behaviour of the operator norm of $\Sigma_{W}^{-1/2}{\bm{W}}^{T}{\bm{W}}\Sigma_{W}^{-1/2}$ .

#### Lemma 17.

Under Assumption 1, with probability $1-2e^{-cK}$ , one has

$$ {1\over n}\left\|\Sigma_{W}^{-1/2}{\bm{W}}^{T}{\bm{W}}\Sigma_{W}^{-1/2}\right\|_{op}\leq 1+C\left(\sqrt{K\over n}\vee{K\over n}\right) $$

where $c=c(\gamma_{w})$ and $C=C(\gamma_{w})$ are positive constants.

The result follows directly from the proof of Theorem 5.39 in [55]. ∎

The following lemma states the deviation inequality of $\|n^{-1}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\|_{F}$ .

#### Lemma 18.

Under Assumption 1, one has

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{\left\|{1\over n}{\bm{\varepsilon}}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}}-\Sigma_{\varepsilon}\right\|_{F}\leq cV_{\varepsilon}\left(\sqrt{\log(m)\over n}\vee{\log(m)\over n}\right)\right\}\geq 1-2m^{-c^{\prime}} $$

for some absolute constants $c,c^{\prime}>0$ .

Fix any $j,\ell\in[m]$ . We first upper bound $|n^{-1}{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{\ell}-(\Sigma_{\varepsilon})_{j\ell}|$ . Since entries of ${\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}$ and ${\bm{\varepsilon}}_{\ell}$ are $\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}}$ and $\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{\ell}}$ sub-Gaussian, respectively, from Lemma 13, invoking Lemma 15 in [9] with $t=\min\{\sqrt{\log(m)/n}\vee\log(m)/n\}$ gives

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{\left|{1\over n}{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}^{T}{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{\ell}-(\Sigma_{\varepsilon})_{j\ell}\right|\leq c\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}}\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{\ell}}\left(\sqrt{\log(m)\over n}\vee{\log(m)\over n}\right)\right\}\geq 1-2m^{-c^{\prime}} $$

for some absolute constants $c,c^{\prime}>0$ . The result then follows by taking the union bounds over $1\leq j,\ell\leq m$ and noting that $\sum_{j}\sum_{\ell}\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{j}}^{2}\gamma_{{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{\ell}}^{2}=V_{\varepsilon}^{2}$ . ∎

### C.7 An algebraic fact and one auxillary lemma

We first state an algebraic fact that is used in our analysis.

#### Fact 1.

Let $Q_{\lambda_{2}}$ be defined in (2.4). Then

$$ Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}=\lambda_{2}{\bm{X}}(\widehat{\Sigma}+\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}. $$

The proof follows by noting that

$$ Q_{\lambda_{2}}{\bm{X}}={\bm{X}}-{\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1}{\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}=n\lambda_{2}{\bm{X}}({\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}+n\lambda_{2}{\bm{I}}_{p})^{-1} $$

and the definition $\widehat{\Sigma}={\bm{X}}^{T}{\bm{X}}/n$ . ∎

The following lemma is used in our analysis. The tail inequality is for a quadratic form of sub-Gaussian random vector. It is a slightly simplified version of Lemma 8 in [38].

#### Lemma 19.

Let $\xi\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be a $\gamma_{\xi}$ sub-Gaussian random vector. For all symmetric positive semidefinite matrices $K$ , and all $t\geq 0$ ,

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{\xi^{T}K\xi>\gamma_{\xi}^{2}\left(\sqrt{{\rm tr}(K)}+\sqrt{2\|K\|_{op}t}\right)^{2}\right\}\leq e^{-t}. $$

From Lemma 8 in [38], one has

$$ \mathbb{P}\left\{\xi^{T}K\xi>\gamma_{\xi}^{2}\left(\textrm{tr}(K)+2\sqrt{\textrm{tr}(K^{2})t}+2\|K\|_{op}t\right)\right\}\leq e^{-t}, $$

for all $t\geq 0$ . The result then follows from $\textrm{tr}(K^{2})\leq\|K\|_{op}\textrm{tr}(K)$ . ∎

## D Comparison of the multivariate ridge estimation and the reduced-rank estimation

### D.1 Comparison with the reduced-rank estimator

In this section, we state our reasoning for using the ridge penalty in (2.3) rather than the commonly used low-rank approach. In particular, we compare our estimator (2.3), or equivalently the multivariate ridge regression, with the reduced-rank estimator under our model (1.4), $Y=(L^{*})^{T}X+(B^{*})^{T}W+E$ when $\Psi^{*}=0$ . Since $L^{*}=A^{*}B^{*}$ exhibits a low-rank structure when both $p$ and $m$ are relatively large comparing to $K$ , one could estimate $L^{*}$ by the reduced-rank estimator [39, 40, 16]

$$ \widehat{L}^{(RR)}=\arg\min_{L}\left\|{\bm{Y}}-{\bm{X}}L\right\|_{F}^{2}+\mu\cdot\textrm{rank}(L) $$

for some tuning parameter $\mu>0$ .

There have been extensive research on the estimation of a low-rank matrix in both regression and matrix completion settings, for instance, [11, 16, 17, 21, 20, 51, 50, 32, 33, 49, 48, 41, 58], a list that is far from exhaustive. In regression setting, the reduced-rank estimator $\widehat{L}^{(RR)}$ is shown to be optimal for both prediction and estimation in high-dimensional settings [16]. Despite of its popularity, we give several reasons why the multivariate ridge-type estimator is more suitable in our setting.

First, we focus on the comparison of the convergence rate of prediction error. Suppose part (b) of Assumption 2 holds. From Corollary 5, by using $s_{*}=0$ , $V_{\varepsilon}=O(Km)$ and $\sum_{k}\sigma_{k}\leq q\sigma_{1}$ with $q=\textrm{rank}({\bm{X}})$ , one can deduce that our estimator ${\bm{X}}\widehat{F}$ satisfies (notice that $F^{*}=L^{*}$ as $\Psi^{*}=0$ )

$$ {1\over n}\left\|{\bm{X}}\widehat{F}-{\bm{X}}L^{*}\right\|_{F}^{2}\lesssim{\sigma_{1}qKm\over\lambda_{2}n}+{\sigma_{1}Km\log(m/\epsilon)\over\lambda_{2}n}+\lambda_{2}\|L^{*}\|_{F}^{2}. $$

When $\log(m)=O(q)$ , choosing $\epsilon=m^{-1}$ and optimizing the above rate over $\lambda_{2}$ yield

$$ {1\over n}\left\|{\bm{X}}\widehat{F}-{\bm{X}}L^{*}\right\|_{F}^{2}\lesssim\sqrt{\sigma_{1}Kqm\over n}\|L^{*}\|_{F}. $$

On the other hand, [16] showed that the reduced-rank estimator $\widehat{L}^{(RR)}$ in (D.1) has the following prediction error

$$ \displaystyle{1\over n}\left\|{\bm{X}}\widehat{L}^{(RR)}-{\bm{X}}L^{*}\right\|_{F}^{2} \displaystyle\lesssim{K\over n}\left\|{\bm{W}}B^{*}+{\bm{E}}\right\|_{op}^{2} \displaystyle\lesssim{Km\over n}\left\|({\bm{W}}B^{*}+{\bm{E}})\Sigma_{\varepsilon}^{-1/2}\right\|_{op}^{2}\lesssim{K(n+m)m\over n} $$

where the first inequality can be proved in the same way as [41, 16], the second inequality holds because the operator norm of $\Sigma_{\varepsilon}=(B^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}+\tau^{2}{\bm{I}}_{m}$ is of order $m$ under part (b) of Assumption 2, and the last inequality is due to the deviation bounds of the operator norm of random matrices whose rows are i.i.d. sub-Gaussian random vectors [55]. Clearly, by $\|L^{*}\|_{F}^{2}\leq K\|L^{*}\|_{op}^{2}$ and recalling that $q=\textrm{rank}({\bm{X}})\leq\min\{n,p\}$ , the rate of our estimator ${\bm{X}}\widehat{F}$ is potentially faster if

$$ {\sigma_{1}\|L^{*}\|_{op}^{2}}\leq{nm\over q}\left(1+{m\over n}\right)^{2} $$

which usually holds, especially when $m$ is large (see the discussion on $\|L^{*}\|_{F}$ in Section 3.4).

To the best of our knowledge, the reduced-rank estimator only achieves the minimax rate when the error covariance matrix has a bounded operator norm [41, 51]. However, as shown above, the error in our model (1.4) has covariance matrix $(B^{*})^{T}\Sigma_{W}B^{*}+\tau^{2}{\bm{I}}_{m}$ whose operator norm is order of $m$ . In this case, the reduced-rank estimator is no longer optimal. Instead, our ridge type estimator leverages the fact that $\|L^{*}\|_{F}$ is small and leads to a much faster prediction rate. This theoretical comparison is further corroborated by simulation studies in Appendix D.2.

Finally, from computational perspective, if we replace $\lambda_{2}\|L\|_{F}^{2}$ in (2.3) by the rank penalty $\lambda_{2}\cdot\textrm{rank}(L)$ , the resulting optimization becomes non-convex and is computationally challenging. For computational convenience, one may instead penalize the nuclear norm of $L$ rather than its rank such that the resulting optimization problem can be solved by the ADMM algorithm. However, to establish statistical guarantees for the corresponding estimator, on top of the RE condition for the group-lasso penalty, this approach may require additional conditions on the design matrix due to the nuclear norm regularization [41]. In contrast, the proposed estimator (2.3) can be computed efficiently and has much weaker restrictions on the design matrix for provable guarantees.

### D.2 Empirical comparison with the reduced-rank estimator

In this section, we compare the multivariate ridge regression with the reduced-rank estimator under model ${\bm{Y}}={\bm{X}}L+{\bm{W}}B+{\bm{E}}$ when $\Psi=\Theta=0$ . Comparing to the commonly studied low-rank regression in the literature, the noise level here is much larger since it follows a factor structure with diverging eigenvalues.

In the following we will demonstrate the advantage of using the multivariate ridge regression in (2.3) with $\lambda_{1}=0$ over the reduced-rank estimator. We first show that the ridge-type estimator has smaller PMSE than the reduced-rank estimator when $\|L\|_{F}$ is small or moderate.
